title: “Good memories of this stadium”: Micho and Christo ahead of Como clash
description: RBL are back in the Champions League! The Red Bulls begin their league-phase campaign away to Como 1907 on Thursday evening (21:00 CEST). It will be the first competitive meeting between the two sides...
fullText:
RBL are back in the Champions League! The Red Bulls begin their league-phase campaign away to Como 1907 on Thursday evening (21:00 CEST). It will be the first competitive meeting between the two sides, and Como are preparing to make their Champions League debut.

Martín Demichelis and Christopher Nkunku spoke to the media on Wednesday evening ahead of the game. How are they feeling about RBL's return to European action? What kind of challenge will Como pose? And what will our game plan be?

We've rounded up the key quotes from the player and head coach.

"My first game as a head coach in the Champions League being here in Como is particularly special for me and a huge honour. I have a strong connection to Italy. My grandmother was Italian. I also did my coaching badges here and I've made a lot of friends in the country.We're coming up against a very good side, so we'll need to be fully focused and trust in our own strengths while also being aware of Como's qualities. We've worked very hard over the past few months and now we want to show that we're ready for this challenge."

"It's nice to be back here. I've got good memories of this stadium. We won here with Milan. I played well and scored.Tomorrow will be a completely different game, though. Como are a very good side. They play an intriguing style of football and move the ball very well. You can see that their players have a very good understanding of how they want to play. We'll need to be fully switched on from the first minute. I'm looking forward to it."

"Micho helps us a lot, both on and off the pitch. We've had a few good days to prepare for the game and he's said the right things to make sure we're fully focused. Hopefully we can earn him three points in his first Champions League game. Of course, we also want to earn the points for ourselves as a team and for everyone in Leipzig. That's our main aim for tomorrow.I had some really good conversations with him before I came back to Leipzig. I knew I wanted to come back here. I wanted to return to RBL and play the kind of football I want to play once again."

"We'll see if I've packed a balloon (laughs). Seriously, though, I'd obviously be delighted if I could help the team with a goal. But ultimately it's about us putting in a good performance and getting the win. That's our aim for tomorrow. It doesn't matter who scores the goals."

title: Yankees linked to 29-HR Jazz Chisholm Jr. replacement in free agency
description: This free-agent second baseman would be a good replacement for Chisholm.
fullText:
Yankees linked to 29-HR Jazz Chisholm Jr. replacement in free agency originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

This upcoming offseason, the New York Yankees are going to have some work to do, especially when it comes to figuring out their infield conundrum.

The left side at shortstop and third base is an issue, but with Jazz Chisholm Jr. set to become a free agent, the second base spot is also a problem. But instead of re-signing Chisholm, the Yankees could look for a replacement.

Mike Axisa of CBS Sports linked the Yankees as a potential landing spot for one 29-homer free-agent second baseman who could replace Chisholm. This veteran slugger is Pittsburgh Pirates All-Star Brandon Lowe.

"One of only 16 players with a 100 OPS+ every season since 2018, Lowe is a middle infielder with 30-homer power," Axisa writes. "...The team that signs Lowe will be the team that believes most in his defensive improvement this year."

Lowe has not been a below-average hitter in nearly a decade. Plus, his recent defensive improvement has made him a lot more intriguing for many teams.

Axisa identified two teams that could make sense as landing spots for Lowe this upcoming offseason: "Super early possible landing spots: Pirates, Yankees."

Chisholm is a good player, but someone like Lowe has a real chance to be a difference-maker for the Yankees if they add his bat to their lineup.

MORE: How Reds' Sal Stewart has MLB history on his side for NL Rookie of the Year award

This season he has posted 4.5 bWAR with 29 homers and a .258 batting average with an .805 OPS. His 116 OPS+ is nothing overly impressive, but it's a good-enough mark that he'd be an appealing target this winter in free agency.

With Chisholm hitting the open market after the 2026 season, the Yankees might need to be in the market for his replacement if he signs elsewhere.

Lowe would be one of the best options they could pursue, as his power is a bit more appealing than someone like Luis Arraez, who, while the NL's batting average leader, doesn't hit for power.

Axisa linking the Yankees to Lowe is a very interesting fit, as the left-handed hitting second baseman would fill the offensive void if Chisholm leaves, or if the Yankees want to shake things up at second base.

title: NDSU Quarterback Nathan Hayes Tasked With 1 Major Job vs. Air Force
description: North Dakota State Bison junior quarterback Nathan Hayes will need to adjust things significantly against Air Force on Saturday. The post NDSU Quarterback Nathan Hayes Tasked With 1 Major Job vs. Air Force appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
North Dakota State Bison junior quarterback Nathan Hayes has been effective through two games as a first-year starter thus far, and he has a new big task ahead of him.

Hayes will need to control time of possession against Air Force on Saturday in the Mountain West Conference opener. That's because Air Force is traditionally a top-five rushing team that is notorious for keeping the ball most of the game.

NDSU head coach Tim Polasek wants Hayes to keep drives extra long to offset Air Force. The Bison possessed the ball for 36:07 in the opener against Jacksonville State and 33:27 against Fordham, and those amounts might not be enough against the Falcons.

"I think at one point I said, 'Nathan, you understand, eight possessions a game,'" Polasek told reporters on Tuesday.

Air Force averaged 33:52 for time of possession last season, and the Falcons kept the ball for 40:50 in the season opener against Duquesne. The Falcons rushed for 431 yards in the 34-0 blowout win over the FCS school, and Air Force has little trouble using the same formula against any team.

​For Polasek, the Falcons are a familiar team from his time on Wyoming's coaching staff in the early 2020s. Wyoming split those games with the Falcons in his time with the Cowboys.

"We think this [Air Force] team's like the ones they had in 2022 and 2023, they were 10-3," Polasek said. "In those years, their opponents averaged about eight possessions a game while they averaged 10; 58 plays to 68, 51 plays to 73 plays. Is that putting pressure on him? You bet."

"We have to go out there, and we have to value every possession that we get offensively, and we've got to go out there and get the first first down, and we've got to have some productivity so our defense doesn't get sent out there too fast," Polasek continued. "Then scoring points is going to be critical."

​Polasek admitted that he has put in extra time and technology into game planning for Air Force, the first-ever Mountain West game in NDSU history. The Bison moved up to the FBS from the FCS after a dominant 15-year run with the invitation from the Mountain West, and Polasek wants things to start off the right way in Colorado Springs.

"I've never looked at analytics as much as I've looked at it for this matchup in the last two to three months," Polasek said. "Just meaning like what does it mean points per possession, what does that mean for wins? They've won the toss 15 times last year and 2023 and they deferred every time."

"I think whether we choose the ball or not are huge decisions. This will be a team win if and when we can get it done," Polasek added. "It'll be because the team plays well. I'd be shocked if we're in here just talking about one unit playing great and the other unit really not playing very good. It'll take everybody, hands on deck, including special teams."

title: Red Sox’s Kristian Campbell Move Gets Attention, but Turns Out to Be False Alarm
description: The Boston Red Sox have a great team going into the postseason. But two fan favorites who have helped Boston succeed in the past still haven’t been recalled. Kristian Campbell and Romy González have been scorching hot in Triple-A Worcester.So naturally, when Campbell and González were taken out midway through Tuesday’s game, it made fans think […] The post Red Sox’s Kristian Campbell Move Gets Attention, but Turns Out to Be False Alarm appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
The Boston Red Sox have a great team going into the postseason. But two fan favorites who have helped Boston succeed in the past still haven't been recalled.

Kristian Campbell and Romy González have been scorching hot in Triple-A Worcester.

So naturally, when Campbell and González were taken out midway through Tuesday's game, it made fans think they were being promoted to the Red Sox.

However, according to MassLive's Christopher Smith, both were removed for precautionary reasons related to injury.

While this doesn't mean the two won't be called up before the season ends, it isn't the case quite yet.

According to Smith, González was dealing with an arm injury, and Campbell was dealing with a toe injury. Neither should miss time due to this.

Both Campbell and González have been red-hot in Worcester. Campbell has slashed .375/.447/.719 with three home runs, 11 RBIs, five walks and two doubles over his last nine games played.

Over González's last 15 games, he has slashed .421/.477/.649 with three home runs, 17 RBIs, seven walks, four doubles and 11 runs scored.

Campbell, despite his former top prospect status, has yet to step on the field for Boston this season. In 67 games during 2025, Campbell slashed .223/.319/.345 with six home runs, 21 RBIs, 29 walks and 10 doubles.

González, on the other hand, never had the top prospect status Campbell had. The Chicago White Sox selected González in the 18th round of the 2018 MLB Draft. Boston would acquire González after 86 major league games with Chicago, and he would thrive.

González would break out in 2025 with a .305/.343/.483 slash line with nine home runs, 53 RBIs, 18 walks and 23 doubles. He did exceptionally well against left-handers, setting him up nicely for the 2026 season.

However, injuries would lead to González not debuting until June 28th, playing just 19 games before Boston sent him down again. He has slashed .185/.264/.308 this season.

While Campbell and González are playing extremely well with Worcester, do they deserve a call-up?

This Red Sox team has been excellent since the All-Star break with a 32-17 record. They are surging towards the playoffs thanks to outstanding pitching and clutch offense.

So, why do fans want Campbell and González up? Barring injuries, it's unlikely either will come back to the team.

When it comes to González especially, the Red Sox have someone filling that role already.

Jahmai Jones is the Red Sox's biggest lefty killer right now. In 26 games since Boston picked him up, Jones has slashed an unbelievable .421/.532/.816 slash line with three home runs. He has played almost exclusively against lefties and has excelled in that role.

As an infielder or designated hitter, both González and Campbell will struggle to get their roles back from Nick Sogard, Andruw Monasterio, Mickey Gasper, Isiah Kiner-Falefa and Eli White. Of all those names, Monasterio could be the odd man out if Boston decides to move one or both of González or Campbell up.

In 99 games, Monasterio is slashing .241/.301/.386 with horrible defense. Sogard, Gasper, Kiner-Falefa, and White have all been hot of late, not leaving much room for either to come up.

It could be a fight until the end of the season for Campbell and González to make an impact at the major league level.

title: ‘So poor’ – Liverpool player slammed for costly moment which left Ally McCoist ‘staggered’
description: Liverpool suffered an all too familiar case of deja vu in tonight’s Champions League clash against Atletico Madrid at Anfield.The visitors broke the deadlock in the 17th minute through a rather unsu...
fullText:
Liverpool suffered an all too familiar case of deja vu in tonight's Champions League clash against Atletico Madrid at Anfield.

The visitors broke the deadlock in the 17th minute through a rather unsurprising source, with Marcos Llorente scoring at this stadium for the fifth time since March 2020.

The Spaniard burst beyond Milos Kerkez into a gap in the Reds defence to get on the end of a through ball from Julian Alvarez and then finish one-on-one past Alisson Becker from the edge of the penalty area.

As Llorente celebrated yet another goal at Anfield, the inquest begun from a Liverpool perspective, and one reporter pointed the finger of blame at the Hungarian left-back.

Aadam Patel of BBC Sport observed: 'Marcos Llorente actually named his dog Anfield. It's a good finish from the Spaniard but the defending is so poor from Milos Kerkez. He has to track his man better.'

Speaking on co-commentary for TNT Sports, Ally McCoist felt that the Reds were culpable as a unit for allowing Atletico's number 14 far too much room in which to score, saying: "I'm staggered at the space they're allowed in the middle of the park. It's absolutely amazing."

(Photo by Michael Regan/Getty Images)

As Alvarez surged towards the halfway line, Liverpool appeared to hold a good defensive shape, but a lack of pressure on the Argentine in midfield allowed him to pick his pass to Llorente.

The Atletico wing-back was much more alert than Kerkez, who was caught flat-footed as the Reds' tormentor in chief burst from behind him and was played through on goal, unsurprisingly making no mistake thereafter.

It was a costly lapse in concentration from the 22-year-old, although the defence as a whole left far too much space for Llorente to get his shot away and score past Alisson.

Liverpool managed to restore parity shortly before the interval thanks to a coolly-taken equaliser from Dominik Szoboszlai, although the manner of the opening goal for the visitors will have stung Andoni Iraola.

title: What Carson Hocevar said about Brad Keselowski's threat and Denny Hamlin's podcast comments
description: Carson Hocevar said he and Brad Keselowski were running hard and Keselowski was trying to hold him off when contact was made at Darlington.
fullText:
Carson Hocevar offered a more detailed explanation but did not come close to apologizing for what happened when he made contact with Brad Keselowski in the NASCAR Darlington race on Sept. 6.

Hocevar didn't have much to say after the race, in which he went from 34th to 11th, about the incident when he spun Keselowski out late in Stage 1. Only "He just spun."

Keselowski vowed retaliation after the race.

After taking more time to review what happened, Hocevar said on Sept. 9 that he and Keselowski had been racing hard for several laps coming to Turn 4. He said Keselowski was trying to block him, suggesting Keselowski was equally responsible for the contact.

CARSON HOCEVAR SPINS BRAD KESELOWSKI: Carson Hocevar spins out Brad Keselowski in Stage 1 of NASCAR Darlington race

"Sometimes (expletive) happens," Hocevar said. "I wasn't trying to spin him out or wreck him, but I was trying to pass him and getting closer and closer, trying to pack air and make his life a little more difficult. Brad did a really good job of holding me off. I think Brad knew how aggressive he was being, racing super hard, trying to keep us behind him."

Hocevar said what happened between him and Keselowski was not out of the norm when racing becomes as intense as it did at that point.

"After 10 or 15 laps of, not patience running out, because it sounds like I was just trying to turn him after 15 laps and I'm like, 'Alright, I'm done with you,'" Hocevar said. "It's more so of, when you're racing really, really tight, within an inch of each other ... it just starts to add to the intensity. Sometimes you just hit. I've been hit multiple times in races throwing blocks ... you just kind of open yourself up to that."

Hocevar has been criticized for his aggressive style over the last few days. Jamie McMurray said on the latest episode of the Door Bumper Clear podcast that Hocevar is "in the bottom handful of racing IQ guys in the field. He just continues to make poor decisions."

Denny Hamlin said he would not talk about his feelings about Hocevar on Hamlin's Actions Detrimental podcast because he did not want to give him the attention that Hocevar craves.

Hocevar shrugged off the critiques, but admitted they could affect those he cares about.

"I just care what (Spire Motorsports co-owner) Jeff (Dickerson), the sponsors, and my team says," Hocevar said. "Whether their opinion changes because of what Brad or Denny or any of these guys think, that's relevant. That's all included. So then I do care. But I think ultimately, racing is a family sport and this is a family and I just care what my family thinks."

Keselowski threatened payback after the race. He told Above the Yellow Line Media that "His day's coming and it's coming hard. Watch out Carson."

Lots of drivers over the years have issued those types of warnings, but few followed through. Hocevar believes this one could be different.

"I mean Corey Heim dumped me at San Diego. Zane (Smith) tried at Chicago," Hocevar said. "So I feel like people have gotten a shot off."

Hocevar said he has not spoken to Keselowski since the Darlington race.

"I don't like the BS apologies, and I think you just race," Hocevar said. "We're just both racing hard. I think he knew what he was doing. He's smart. He's won a championship. He knows how hard he's racing and trying to hold us off."

title: ‘People in the White House hate the story of immigrants’: Criticism mounts for the Trump administration after legendary US Open result
description: Frances Tiafoe, a Maryland native, defeated Alex Michelsen in a hard-fought four-hour match last night to advance to the semifinals of the US Open. Tiafoe rallied from down two sets and managed to overcome Michelsen, 7-5, 6-3, 7-6(10-6), in the next three sets, finishing victorious. Michelsen and Tiafoe shared a long embrace after the match,…
fullText:
Frances Tiafoe, a Maryland native, defeated Alex Michelsen in a hard-fought four-hour match last night to advance to the semifinals of the US Open. Tiafoe rallied from down two sets and managed to overcome Michelsen, 7-5, 6-3, 7-6(10-6), in the next three sets, finishing victorious. Michelsen and Tiafoe shared a long embrace after the match, as the two are good friends and share mutual respect on the court. A picture-perfect moment for media figures as a black competitor shows compassion to a fellow white American opponent.

Although Tiafoe was American-born, he has often spoken about his parents, who escaped the Civil War in Sierra Leon and fled to the US in 1990. He has often mentioned the sacrifices his parents made for him and his brother, as his father, Constant Tiafoe, worked as a day laborer on a construction crew building the Junior Tennis Champions Center (JTCC) in College Park, Maryland, and his mother, Alphina, worked as a nurse. Their immigrant background left room for MS NOW reporters to tie the Trump administration's reluctance toward migrants into the triumph Tiafoe had Wednesday night.

Morning Joe on Frances Tiafoe advancing in the U.S. Open: “For some reason, some people in the White House hate the story of immigrants coming from places they call shitholes & becoming great Americans, that are great examples for our own children.” pic.twitter.com/6szS2ZdEZq

— Tom Elliott (@tomselliott) September 9, 2026

"For some reason, some people in the White House hate the story of immigrants coming from places they call sh*thole countries and becoming great Americans that are great examples for our own children," Joe Scarborough of Morning Joe said.

"What's the origin of the story? The origin of the story is a country in distant Africa. Whats the fulmination, the culmination of the story? The culmination of the story is in the United States of America, by a young man…look at him, he represents America, that's what America is all about," Mike Barniclesaid.

"The tragedy of the Trump administration, both administrations, is they have spent now a decade together, four years out of office, but a decade running this country down. They pose as great patriots. They pose as if we're going to make America strong again; we're going to bring back America. Nobody has to bring back America; the United States of America is the greatest goddamn country on Earth. People don't travel; they don't realize it, but it is."

The classic Trump slogan from his first presidential campaign, "Make America Great Again," caused nationwide chaos as voters on both sides feuded, visibly dividing states. Any supporter of the United States president is now issued the MAGA tag next to their name, a stamp Barnicle found unnecessary to begin with.

Tiafoe's next matchup is against another American opponent, Ben Shelton. No matter the outcome, the US will be a participant in the 2026 US Open final.

title: Aaron Rodgers Explains Why He Thinks Steelers are Super Bowl Contender
description: Steelers QB Aaron Rodgers believes he can go out on top.
fullText:
Aaron Rodgers Explains Why He Thinks Steelers are Super Bowl Contender originally appeared on SportsNet Pittsburgh. Add SportsNet Pittsburgh as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

It's year 22 in the NFL for Aaron Rodgers and, by all indications, it will be his last.

Rodgers has made it clear he won't play beyond this season, so how the Steelers finish is 2026 is how he will finish his career. If you ask Rodgers, he isn't willing to put a ceiling on the team.

Asked by SiriusXM's Adam Schein whether the Steelers are a Super Bowl contender, Rodgers responded affirmatively.

"Yeah, of course. Of course. That's why I came back, because I believe in the guys," Rodgers said, singling out additions Jamal Dean, Jaquan Brisker, Sebastian Joseph-Day and the organization's rookies.

"We still have dynamic pass rushers ... our defensive line is one of the bigger d-lines I've been a part of," Rodgers said "I like the depth on the defensive side of the ball."

"I like the roster as a whole," Rodgers said. "We have good veteran leadership. It's just about going out there and doing it."

Are the #Steelers Super Bowl contenders this season?

"Yeah, of course. That's why I came back." @AaronRodgers12 tells @AdamSchein why he believes Pittsburgh can make a run to the Super Bowl. pic.twitter.com/FfaXT4XiZf

Rodgers admitted the AFC is "very deep," with Super Bowl contenders sharing a division with the Steelers, but his message was clear: the right roster has been assembled, and it's now up to the players to execute.

The Steelers last won a playoff game in 2016, so they are at the very least hoping to prevent that drought from stretching to 10 seasons in 2026 as Rodgers plays out his final NFL campaign.

description: Four-star Chase Lumpkin, one of the top combo guards in the 2027 class, has committed to Alabama, he told Rivals. The 6-foot-4 senior out of McEachern (GA) chose the Crimson Tide over offers from Arkansas, Kentucky, Louisville, Michigan, and USC. Lumpkin is ranked as the No. 26 overall recruit in the 2027 class and the No. […]
fullText:
Four-star Chase Lumpkin, one of the top combo guards in the 2027 class, has committed to Alabama, he told Rivals.

The 6-foot-4 senior out of McEachern (GA) chose the Crimson Tide over offers from Arkansas, Kentucky, Louisville, Michigan, and USC.

Lumpkin is ranked as the No. 26 overall recruit in the 2027 class and the No. 9 ranked point guard, according to the Rivals Industry Ranking, an average of all three major recruiting media companies (Rivals, ESPN, 247Sports).

[ $19.99 gets you a FULL year of On3 | Rivals national coverage ]

Chase Lumpkin went in-depth on his decision to choose 'Bama with Rivals.

"Alabama just felt like the right fit for me and my family. I really connected with Coach Oats, Coach Murphy, and the whole staff. They've always kept it real with me and made me feel like they genuinely wanted me there."

Lumpkin believes Alabama is an ideal fit for his style of play.

"I love the way they play and the culture they're building, and I feel like my game fits really well within their system. The new facility and technology they have for player development is also second to none. I know those resources will help me keep improving and reach my goals.

"When I put everything together, Alabama just felt like home, and I knew it was where I wanted to be."

Coach Nate Oats and assistant coach Preston Murphy made Lumpkin a priority throughout his recruitment and stayed consistent with him and his family.

"I have a really good relationship with Coach Oats, Coach Murphy, and the whole staff. They were at almost every game I played this summer, and that meant a lot to me because it shows how much they believe in me.

"Coach Murphy was a huge part of my recruitment. He stayed consistent with me and my family and really took the time to get to know me beyond basketball. Coach Oats has also been great. I really like how honest he is with me and how he pushes me to get better.

"I trust both of them, and I'm definitely excited to play for them and be part of what they're building at Alabama."

Lumpkin also described the type of player Alabama is getting.

"I'd describe myself as a versatile guard who can impact the game in a lot of ways. I can score at all three levels, create for myself and my teammates, defend multiple positions, and play with pace.

"One of my biggest strengths is reading the game and making the right play. I try to play with confidence, bring energy on both ends, and do whatever my team needs to win. I'm always working on becoming a more consistent defender and improving every part of my game."

Lumpkin also shared a message for Alabama fans:

"Tuscaloosa, I'm coming ready to work, compete, win, and leave my mark. Roll Tide!!"

Rivals national recruiting analyst Jamie Shaw has evaluated Lumpkin multiple times in person this summer. Here is what he's written about the highly regarded guard:

"Lumpkin is very confident on the ball. He has good feet and solid positional size in the 6-foot-4 range. He shot the cover off the ball, stepping into shots and knocking down catch and shoots. Also showed passing acumen, delivering on target and on time as a primary initiator. Lumpkin played a streamlined and confident game. He got to spots and put consistent pressure on the opposing team. Lumpkin finished with 29 points and 8 assists on 8 of 15 shooting in the Jet Academy win.

"Lumpkin was the breakout player of the weekend. The Jet Academy guard did a little bit of everything for his team, initiating offense, finishing plays, and generally creating advantages for his team. He showcased excellent vision on the ball, and he processed quickly and efficiently, whether that was getting the ball to his teammates or making shots on his own accord. Lumpkin got into the paint consistently, and he finished well at the rim."

This summer on the Nike EYBL Circuit, Lumpkin averaged 17.3 points, 5.7 rebounds, 4.5 assists, and 2.2 steals per game for Jet Academy.

title: Dembélé roars back to form with 2 first-half goals and an assist against Slovan in Champions League
description: Ballon d'Or winner Ousmane Dembélé scored titleholder Paris Saint-Germain's first goals of the new Champions League campaign, and his first goals the season, when he netted twice in the first half against Slovan Bratislava on Wednesday.  It was a welcome return to form for Dembélé, one of France's World Cup stars with six goals, following a frustrating start to the domestic season.
fullText:
PARIS (AP) — Ballon d'Or winner Ousmane Dembélé scored titleholder Paris Saint-Germain's first goals of the new Champions League campaign, and his first goals the season, when he netted twice in the first half against Slovan Bratislava on Wednesday.

He also set up a goal for new signing Ferran Torres as PSG led 3-0 at the break.

It was a welcome return to form for Dembélé, one of France's World Cup stars with six goals, following a frustrating start to the domestic season.

He was taken off at halftime in PSG's Ligue 1 opener after a lackluster performance against Rennes in a 2-2 draw, and was then left out of the next game against Lille by coach Luis Enrique. Dembélé was ineffective as a late second-half substitute in a 2-1 home loss to Monaco last Friday.

Dembélé put PSG ahead in the 17th minute against Slovan, reacting quickly after Nuno Mendes' swerving shot hit the post and steering the rebound inside the right post.

He clipped a shot wide from just inside the left of the penalty area moments later, before heading in his second goal in the 23rd from 18-year-old midfielder Dro Fernandez's right-wing cross.

Dembélé then set up Torres, who drifted in to meet his cross from the right for his third goal since joining from Barcelona, after scoring the winner in the World Cup final for Spain.

Dembélé dropped to his knees in frustration when he somehow hit the crossbar from close range on the half-hour mark as PSG sliced Slovan apart. Ten PSG players were nominated Tuesday on the shortlist of 30 for the Ballon d'Or, which Dembélé won for the first time last year.

Before facing Slovan at Parc des Princes, PSG had failed to win its previous four games, conceding seven goals and losing the French Super Cup to Lens.

As Bradley Barcola started in attack for new club Liverpool, his replacement Maghnes Akliouche took the field for PSG alongside Torres and Dembélé.

Another star of PSG's Champions League-winning campaign last season, Khvicha Kvaratskhelia, was on the bench, as Luis Enrique fine-tunes his attack following the departures of Barcola and striker Gonçalo Ramos to AC Milan.

title: Teoscar Hernández says Elly De La Cruz is only one who'd throw him out
description: The Dodgers' Teoscar Hernández praised Reds shortstop Elly De La Cruz for his ridiculous throw to home plate to prevent an inside-the-park home run.
fullText:
The Los Angeles Dodgers' Teoscar Hernández delivered quite a compliment after Cincinnati Reds shortstop Elly De La Cruz made a remarkable throw to home plate, to prevent Hernández from stretching a triple into an inside-the-park home run in the bottom of the third inning Sept. 8 at Dodger Stadium.

"I think he's the only one who can throw me out in that situation," Hernández said of De La Cruz.

Hernández added that it would have been his first inside-the-park home run as a pro at any level, per FOX Sports' Rowan Kavner, and that he thought he was close to scoring until he watched the replay.

"He is a video game character," Reds.TV play-by-play announcer John Sadak said during the broadcast. "He just uncorked a throw that, if this is accurate, Statcast says he threw that ball to home plate … at 105.3 miles per hour! 105.3! Is this man real?"

The Reds reported that the update on the speed of the throw was 102.0 MPH.

"That was one of the better throws you'll ever see. I mean ever," Reds manager Terry Francona said after the game.

This article originally appeared on Cincinnati Enquirer: Teoscar Hernández says Elly De La Cruz is only one who'd throw him out

title: Brock Bowers injury update is awful news for Raiders
description: Las Vegas Raiders tight end Brock Bowers was not spotted at the open portion of practice on Wednesday.
fullText:
The Las Vegas Raiders have a new injury concern on their hands and it comes in the form of star tight end Brock Bowers.

According to The Athletic's Sam Warren, Bowers was not spotted at the portion of practice that is open to the media.

It was later reported that Bowers underwent a meniscus trim on Tuesday and will miss a game or two to start the season, according to ESPN's Adam Schefter.

MORE: Malik Nabers injury update all but confirms Giants WR's Week 1 status

"Raiders All-Pro tight end Brock Bowers underwent a meniscus trim Tuesday in Dallas with Dr. Daniel Cooper and now is expected to miss "a game or two", league sources told (Ian Rapoport) and me," Schefter reported.

Schefter went on to add that Bowers injured during training camp and "the injury was diagnosed last week and surgery scheduled."

While obviously not the worst-case scenario for the Raiders, this is still a significant blow to Las Vegas' offense for as long as Bowers is out.

The Raiders already have a shaky situation with their pass-catchers, so it goes without saying big of a blow this is to the offense.

Bowers rocketed to stardom in his first season in the NFL, when he tallied 112 catches for 1,194 yards and five touchdowns en route to breaking several records.

He was once again very productive last season, but he also missed five games due to injury, which impacted his numbers and led to him finishing with 64 receptio0ns for 680 yards and seven touchdowns.

title: Nkunku ‘surprised’ by Milan sale: ‘I don’t understand why they acted that way’
description: Christopher Nkunku admits he was surprised by Milan’s decision to send him back to RB Leipzig and says he still does not understand why the Rossoneri handled his departure that way.The French forwar...
fullText:
Christopher Nkunku admits he was surprised by Milan's decision to send him back to RB Leipzig and says he still does not understand why the Rossoneri handled his departure that way.

The French forward returned to Leipzig after just one season at Milan, having joined the Italian side from Chelsea in the summer of 2025.

Reflecting on his time between Chelsea and Milan, Nkunku said in comments via Calciomercato.com: "When I went to Chelsea, things started well and then I suffered an injury at the end of the last friendly. After that, everything changed. I had my first operation, I wanted to get back on the pitch quickly and there were also many changes. I didn't like my role at Chelsea.

"At Milan, on the other hand, I didn't have any injuries, but the football philosophy was different from mine. So, as soon as I had the opportunity to come back here and play my football, I took it."

PISA, ITALY – FEBRUARY 13: Christopher Nkuku of AC Milan in action during the Serie A match between Pisa SC and AC Milan at Arena Garibaldi on February 13, 2026 in Pisa, Italy. (Photo by Gabriele Maltinti/Getty Images)

Nkunku was then asked about Milan's decision to let him leave.

"It's a decision that has to be respected, but I didn't understand why they acted that way either. I was surprised. In any case, I wish them a good season."

The 28-year-old is nevertheless happy to have returned to Leipzig.

"I'm very happy to be here and I'm convinced I made the right decision. The first week has been fantastic and the team made me feel very welcome."

MILAN, ITALY – MAY 10: Christopher Nkunku of AC Milan scores his team's second goal from a penalty kick during the Serie A match between AC Milan and Atalanta BC at Giuseppe Meazza Stadium on May 10, 2026 in Milan, Italy. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images)

Nkunku scored seven goals in 32 Serie A appearances last season. Milan have loaned him to Leipzig for €4m, with an option to buy for €28m.

title: Rampant Raphinha bags brace as Barcelona rout Feyenoord
description: Raphinha continued his superb goalscoring form with a brace as Barcelona demolished Feyenoord 5-1 to begin their Champions League campaign in perfect fashion on Wednesday.Adeyemi, in for Anthony Gordon, doubled Barcelona's lead with a superb strike from outside the area, bent beyond Feyenoord goalkeeper Tjark Ernst.
fullText:
Raphinha continued his superb goalscoring form with a brace as Barcelona demolished Feyenoord 5-1 to begin their Champions League campaign in perfect fashion on Wednesday.

Karim Adeyemi curled home brilliantly from long range in between Raphinha's strikes and Lamine Yamal bent in a free-kick as Hansi Flick's team made light work of their Dutch visitors.

After Sem Steijn pulled one back, Barca substitute Gabriel Jesus netted a fifth, the forward's first goal since joining from Arsenal this summer.

The Catalan giants, who last won the competition in 2015, have triumphed in all five of their matches across all competitions this season -- and scored five goals in four of them.

"The first five games, we did really good. We scored a lot of goals but the most important thing is we are playing like a team, like one unit," Flick told reporters.

"We controlled the game, we are dominant and this is fantastic to see. This is our style and how we want to play."

Winger Raphinha has been playing up front after Barca sold Robert Lewandowski and Ferran Torres, and has rapidly taken to his new position, plundering eight goals in five games.

"Playing in front of our fans we always have to show perfect football, or nearly perfect, and with the support of the fans it's a lot easier," Barca captain Raphinha told Movistar.

"I think we were very good, from the start of the game, controlling the game and with the chances we had we were able to score and it gives us a lot of confidence."

The Brazil international said that despite the club's excellent start, there was still a long way to go.

"In a season as long as this, there are many ups and downs," added Raphinha.

"Starting the season like this obviously gives us a lot of confidence and we have to continue like this.

"We have to hope the downs are as small as possible."

After days of baking weather in Barcelona, a storm broke ahead of the game, lashing rain down on the Camp Nou pitch and sending supporters scurrying for shelter.

Raphinha netted the opener after three minutes.

The Brazilian was razor sharp to break into the box and cut inside, sending two defenders sliding the wrong way on the slick turf, before slotting home.

Adeyemi, in for Anthony Gordon, doubled Barcelona's lead with a superb strike from outside the area, bent beyond Feyenoord goalkeeper Tjark Ernst.

Joao Cancelo hit the post before Raphinha netted again in the second half for Barca's third, running on to Pedri's perfect through-ball and slotting home.

The Dutch side thought they had pulled one back straight away when Nacho Ferri slotted home but it was disallowed after a VAR review for offside in the build-up.

Yamal bagged Barca's fourth, direct from a free-kick which crept through the wall, his first such strike for the club.

Feyenoord sent on Shaqueel van Persie, the 19-year-old son of former Dutch international Robin van Persie, to try and salvage some pride.

Steijn eventually pulled one back for the visitors when he escaped Jules Kounde and Goncalo Borges picked him out with a dangerous low cross to the back post.

It was the only blot on Barca's copy book on an otherwise strong start to their league phase, rounded off by Jesus's glancing header from Yamal's cross for the fifth.

title: NFL Week 1 Fantasy Football injury report: Puka Nacua, Malik Nabers, more
description: It’s the time of year when injuries begin to matter in fantasy football , even the lesser ones. And rankings get adjusted on the fly . Furthermore, here is the NFL Week 1 fantasy football injury report, including Puka Nacua and Malik Nabers. It’s tough landing on the injury report heading into Week 1. fullText:
NFL Week 1 Fantasy Football injury report: Puka Nacua, Malik Nabers, more appeared first on ClutchPoints. 

It's the time of year when injuries begin to matter in fantasy football, even the lesser ones. And rankings get adjusted on the fly. Furthermore, here is the NFL Week 1 fantasy football injury report, including Puka Nacua and Malik Nabers.

It's tough landing on the injury report heading into Week 1. But it's inevitable in the NFL that some players won't be able to make a go of it out of the gate. Others will play, but perhaps not at 100%.

Let's take a look at the latest.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

The Rams have cleared Nacua, and he is expected to play against the 49ers. He also has groin soreness, which isn't a concern. Also, he won't face a suspension, according to a post on X by Adam Schefter.

Adam Schefter: "I think there's a real possibility that Puka Nacua doesn't face any discipline this season. He's gonna be out there against the San Francisco 49ers"

Nabers suffered a torn ACL in Week 4 last season. Nabers appears to be ready for the Cowboys, according to a post on X by Get Up.

"It sounds like [Malik Nabers is] going to be good to go for Sunday night."

Expectations are for Kittle to be on the field as the 49ers meet the Rams. He tore his Achilles on Jan. 11, so this is a remarkable timeline if he plays.

It's never good to see multiple. But this is Mike Evans. But Evans said he would have played if the games had been in progress, according to ninersnation.com.

"The training staff, they did a great job working with me," Evans said. "I know I'm an older player. I've had probably over a thousand practices, football practices in my life now, so I know what I'm doing out there. They know what they're doing. They did a good job taking care of me. None of my injuries were significant. If it was a game week, I wouldn't have missed any time."

It has been a long summer for Pierce, but it looks like he has recovered enough to face the Ravens, according to ESPN.

"He should be good to go," Colts head coach Shane Steichen said. "We'll get him some reps and practice this week, just like he took reps last week. He's feeling really good."

It's hard to say how effective Mahomes will be early in the season. But at least he should be able to get on the field, according to ESPN.

"There's a pretty good chance Patrick will go ahead and start, unless something were to come up here in the next couple days," Reid said Tuesday. "Most likely, he'll be the guy out there. Other than having a brace on his leg, everything looks normal. He's running around the same way he's always done. I think he'll be fine there."

The good news is Jeanty appears to have avoided a long-term absence. And now there's hope he will be able to play in Week 1, according to the Raiders YouTube page.

"Head coach Klint Kubiak was asked if he was optimistic about Jeanty playing in the season opener," Tyler Bischoff wrote. "And he gave a one-word answer: Yes."

After missing consecutive practices, Henderson's chances of playing were downgraded. Then on Tuesday evening, the Patriots decided Henderson would not play, according to Patriots.com.

This opens the door for Rhamondre Stevenson to have a much bigger role in the season-opening Super Bowl rematch against the Seahawks.

It looks like Penix needs more time after last year's injury, according to atlantafalcons.com.

"I want to be stronger," Penix said. "I want to be able to be out there and give the team 100%. And if I don't feel like I can do that, that's not fair for this team. That's not fair for this organization. I want to make sure whenever I am out there, I'm 100%, and there's no doubt in my mind that I trust my knee and that I trust being able to go out there and help this team win football games."

There are question marks around Brooks' availability for the opener, according to atozsports.com.

"After practice, head coach Dave Canales said all injury updates will not be addressed until after Wednesday's practice," Kole Noble wrote. "He did (say) he "hopes" Brooks can play, but they're going to evaluate it one day at a time."

It appears Egbuka will give it a go, according to NBC Sports.

"It sounds like Egbuka is trending in the right direction ahead of the Buccaneers' Week 1 game against the Bengals, Zachary Krueger wrote.

It's a process, but Love may be getting close, according to Pro Football Network.

"Jeremiyah Love is still working his way back from the high ankle sprain he suffered on his final touch of the preseason opener against the Las Vegas Raiders," PFN wrote. "Mike LaFleur gave his rookie running back 14 touches in the first half of a game that does not count."

The Bears are still holding out hope that Odunze will be able to get on the field in Week 1. His inability to practice Tuesday perhaps made those hopes dwindle somewhat.

Last week's practice injury put Chase in questionable mode. But he has been able to practice this week.

It looks like Higgins will be able to give it a go.

Reports suggest Shakir will be able to play against the Texans.

In the process of working his way back, the consensus is that Kamara won't suit up for the opener.

title: Roberto Satoshi: RIZIN co-promoting with PFL, MVP opens doors for ‘dream fights’
description: BJJ wiz Roberto Satoshi is a former RIZIN lightweight champion
fullText:
Former RIZIN lightweight champion Roberto Satoshi loves to see the Japanese company co-promote with the Professional Fighters League — and automatically their new partners MVP MMA — and potentially lead to dream fights on North American soil.

The PFL and RIZIN will unify their featherweight title Thursday, when A.J. McKee battles Razhabali Shaydullaev for both 145-pound belts at Super RIZIN 5, and Satoshi hopes it could also happen one day in the heavier weight classes. Satoshi, who faces off with Shunta Nomura on the Sept. 10 card in Osaka, sets sight on the title he once held and possibly matches with PFL talents Usman Nurmagomedov, Paul Hughes, Alexandr Shabliy, and Gadzhi Rabadanov.

"I think it's really cool when you stop and think about the fact that RIZIN is doing is something no other promotion has done," Satoshi told MMA Fighting. "Bringing two promotions together, merging them like that, happens quite often in boxing. Having the world champion from one promotion fight the world champion from another promotion, like A.J. against Shaydullaev, is really good. It's really cool.

"The fighters can only benefit from it, the promotion can only benefit from it, and the fans benefit too, because there are so many matchups we've always dreamed of seeing. How many fights did we imagine back when Bellator was at its strongest, with their champions fighting UFC champions? It would be a dream to be able to fight overseas, in the United States. My entire career has been here in Japan, so it would be really cool."

Another star that is joining RIZIN on this week's show is Shinya Aoki, who returns to the promotion 11 years after his sole appearance before signing with ONE Championship. Satoshi has seen Japanese fans campaign for this match-up for many years in the past and still thinks it could lead to a "very interesting" challenge in grappling, if not under MMA rules.

"People talked about it a lot because when I had the RIZIN belt and he had the ONE belt," Satoshi said. "Then he went through a rough patch, lost two or three fights in a row, and kind of took a step back, but there was a time when people talked about that matchup a lot. There's not much I can say other than he's a legend.

"In Japan, at lightweight, he was the guy who carried Japanese MMA for a very long time," he continued. "He didn't have the best performances when he took a chance and went over to Strikeforce, but there's not much to say, he's a legend. Obviously, he's getting older now, but that doesn't mean his jiu-jitsu isn't still sharp. He still has the name, and he's still the same guy he always was, you know?"

The man standing across the ring Thursday at the Kyosera Dome Osaka arena is Shunta Nomura, who also holds a win over current RIZIN champion Luiz Gustavo. Satoshi said this is the third time RIZIN has paired them up, giving him plenty of time to prepare the ideal strategy.

"I've been studying him for a long time," Satoshi said. "I know he has a tricky style, he uses that karate style, getting in and out, and has very fast movement. But it's a fight that interested me. He's a new prospect coming out of Japan and he's already beaten the two Brazilians in the lightweight division, so it's an interesting fight."

The jiu-jitsu specialist believes that avoiding grappling exchanges is "the game plan of everyone I've fought so far, […] but I've also been training a lot of striking. I've been building my confidence. I think we'll be able to have an interesting fight, not just a striker vs. grappler type of matchup."

RIZIN has yet to announce who's next in line for Gustavo's title, and the winner of Satoshi vs. Nomura would make sense considering both hold wins over the Brazilian knockout artist.

"You could basically call this a title eliminator. Whoever wins has a very good chance of getting a shot at the belt," Satoshi said. "I think this fight is very important because I've become a veteran now. Nomura is one of the younger guys coming up, so I want to show that I still have my place here and that I can still make another run at the belt. This fight is very important for that. If I win, the path to the title becomes much closer and much easier."

title: Why this freshman can fill L.J. Cason’s shoes for Michigan Basketball
description: Michigan Basketball lost L.J. Cason to the transfer portal this offseason, but this freshman for the Wolverines could help fill his shoes this season:
fullText:
Coming off a national championship, the only player in Michigan's rotation to transfer out this offseason was guard L.J. Cason, who left Michigan for Miami following the departure of Dusty May. The Florida native will play for the Hurricanes once he recovers from his torn ACL.

Cason was one of Michigan's most important players last season. In 28 games, Cason averaged 8.4 points, 2.4 assists and 1.9 rebounds in 18.6 minutes per game, serving as one of Michigan's key bench scorers. Since the media first saw him at Michigan's Pro Day two years ago, Cason has had the reputation of being Michigan's best one-on-one scorer. To win games consistently in the Big Ten, you need guys like Cason who can create their own shot when nothing else in the offense is clicking.

Depth will be a huge question for this team heading into the 2026-27 season. After all the roster changes this offseason, Michigan will need to rely on freshmen to contribute off the bench in 2026-27.

Cason's ability to take over games with his microwave scoring ability will be missed, but to paraphrase your mom after you asked to pick up McDonald's for dinner, Michigan may have the next L.J. Cason already at home.

We saw glimpses of what freshman guard Joseph Hartman could do during Michigan's trip to Europe last month. Hartman only made six of his 22 shots, but he showed his prowess as a scorer several times, scoring seven points and six points, respectively, off the bench in Michigan's first two games.

Joseph Hartman stock up despite a pretty modest box score:

6 PTS
2 AST

The numbers don’t really show how comfortable he looked. Confident ball handler, willing passer, can get downhill and create his own shot.

He looks much more polished than his ranking suggested.#GoBlue 〽️ pic.twitter.com/3PwdCjtVRm

In the videos above from Michigan's second exhibition of the trip, Hartman showed off his bucket-getting ability in the fourth quarter, getting to the lane and using his pivot foot to wiggle around defenders for clutch buckets.

The 6-foot-6 guard was a top-100 four-star recruit on the 247Sports composite, and reading the first part of Hartman's scouting report from 247's Adam Finkelstein, Hartman's skillset certainly sounds a lot like Cason's.

"Hartman is built like a strong-bodied wing, but has some big guard type skills. He's a good ball-handler and passer, and can even operate as a jumbo initiator at times. He utilizes his size and strength to take smaller defenders into the mid-post. He can also space the floor as a spot-up shooting threat, knocking down 44% of his threes, on over 4 attempts per game, during the 3SSB season."

Finkelstein went on to say Hartman is "not a dynamic athlete and lacks elite quickness or bounce," two parts of Cason's game that made him a tough cover. But Hartman is four inches taller than Cason, which could help make up for that lack of burst.

Hartman re-affirmed his commitment to the Wolverines in July following May's departure. With rosters mostly set at that point in the summer, Hartman didn't have many other choices, but you'd have to imagine part of his reasoning for staying was having some sort of a role on this year's team.

Is it fair to expect Hartman to immediately average the same amount of points as Cason did last season before his injury? Absolutely not, it usually takes freshman guards some time to get used to the pace of college hoops. But Michigan has a few options to replace Cason's scoring, and Hartman is certainly one of them.

title: Ben Shelton and the four other American players who have defeated Carlos Alcaraz on the ATP Tour
description: Ben Shelton became the fifth player to defeat Carlos Alcaraz on the professional circuit after stunning the Spaniard on Wednesday morning. Shelton, the American number...
fullText:
Ben Shelton became the fifth player to defeat Carlos Alcaraz on the professional circuit after stunning the Spaniard on Wednesday morning.

Shelton, the American number one, triumphed 6-7, 6-3, 6-1, 1-6, 7-6 in the US Open quarter-finals, ending the Spaniard's title defence.

The American superstar, 23, will play compatriot Frances Tiafoe in the US Open semi-finals.

In light of Alcaraz's defeat, let's take a look back at the past occasions in which the Spanish superstar has seen his progress halted by an American player.

Tiafoe, a three-time US Open semi-finalist, was the first American to defeat Carlos Alcaraz on the ATP Tour.

In 2021, Tiafoe and Alcaraz met in the Barcelona Open first round.

Tiafoe emerged victorious, triumphing 6-4, 7-6.

Tiafoe was beaten in the very next round by Diego Schwartzman.

Alcaraz has recorded two victories against Tiafoe since that initial defeat: at the 2022 US Open and 2024 Wimbledon Championships.

Korda is one of only two American players to have recorded multiple victories against Carlos Alcaraz.

The talented American first triumphed over the Spaniard at the 2022 Monte Carlo Masters.

Korda defeated Alcaraz 7-6, 6-7, 6-3 in the second round.

The American also stunned Alcaraz at the 2026 Miami Open.

"It feels great," said Korda, who won 6-3, 5-7, 6-4 in Florida.

"I took the scenic route, that's for sure – a little more stress than I would want but happy with how I played.

"I kept believing. I got myself in some nasty situations, but I kept going and played really well in the end."

Paul has also recorded two victories against Alcaraz.

The New Jersey native first defeated the seven-time major champion at the 2022 Canadian Open.

Paul stunned second-seeded Alcaraz in the second round, 6-7, 7-6, 6-3.

Paul went on to reach the quarter-finals, where he lost to British player Dan Evans.

A year later, Paul triumphed against Alcaraz at the same event.

In the quarter-finals, Paul defeated Alcaraz 6-3, 4-6, 6-3.

"I played a really good match today. I really went after my shots," Paul said. "You can't start any points on your heels against him or he'll take advantage of that.

"So you really have to go after your shots early in the rally and I was feeling really good on the first-strike tennis.

"That was the difference today."

Alcaraz has not participated in the event since.

Fritz, a finalist at the 2024 US Open, has defeated Alcaraz just once in a professional setting.

This triumph occurred at the 2025 Laver Cup – which is not an official ATP Tour event.

However, the victory at the exhibition event is listed in Fritz's head-to-head record against Alcaraz.

The former American number one defeated Alcaraz 6-3, 6-2.

"I think I take almost more pride in this one because I feel like, start to finish, I won it, I earned it," Fritz said afterwards.

"A lot of the decisive points in the match weren't so much him giving them to me – I felt like I made it happen in those moments. Just start to finish, I played an amazing match. I'm hoping this can be a sign of things to come."

The victory helped propel Team World to the 2025 Laver Cup title.

Arsenal have identified Nico Paz as the next top player they want to add to their squad at the end of this season, as he continues to develop well and shine at Como, where he has established himself as one of the top players in Europe.

Paz was on loan at Como last season after joining them from Real Madrid, but he is now their player and wants to continue developing his career at the Italian club.

Paz has been transformed into a top player by Cesc Fabregas, and the midfielder could be a fine addition to the Arsenal squad if the Gunners manage to bring him to the Emirates.

Arsenal see Paz as a player who can make their team stronger than it is at the moment. A report on Sport Witness says the Gunners would look to add him to their squad next season.

Paz has continued to impress with his performances, and his development has made him an attractive option for Arsenal as they consider how to strengthen their squad further.

Como are an ambitious club, while Paz is a top player, so he will not be cheap. Arsenal may still believe he would be attracted to a move to the Emirates, particularly because the Gunners have been one of the top teams in Europe.

(Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images)

It will therefore be interesting to see whether Como would be open to negotiations with Arsenal and whether Paz himself would fancy making the move to the Emirates.

For now, Arsenal appear to view Paz as a player capable of improving their squad. His continued development at Como could make him an increasingly attractive target, but any potential move will depend on whether the relevant parties are willing to explore a deal.

title: NCAA can't overturn WMU-Michigan, but it clarifies timer protocols
description: The MAC filed a formal appeal Tuesday, asking that Michigan's controversial 13-12 win over Western Michigan be overturned.
fullText:
The Mid-American Conference made its point.

And Michigan, no surprise, will keep its points — and, as a result, its 13-12 victory over Western Michigan.

The NCAA has confirmed what always was going to be the resolution: It has no protocol or precedent with which to overturn the controversial result from the football game at Michigan Stadium in Ann Arbor on Saturday, Sept. 5.

The MAC formally filed an appeal with the NCAA and College Football Playoff on Tuesday, Sept. 8, asking for the result to be overturned after Michigan beat Western Michigan on a last-second Hail Mary touchdown. The winning touchdown came after officials put 1 second back on the clock, allowing Michigan one final play.

The MAC, through a statement from commissioner from Jon Steinbrecher, said protocols weren't followed, and appealed to the NCAA, the Division I Football Bowl Subdivision Oversight Committee and the College Football Playoff to intervene, after the fact. The NCAA's official rule book, however, clearly states officials' decisions on the end of games are final, and can't be overturned.

The Big Ten, in the hours after the wild finish to the game in Ann Arbor, released video and audio to the public showing its replay process in allowing Michigan one last second — an explanation that initially satisfied the MAC and Western Michigan, if not all the pundits. The Big Ten used its internal replay-feed clock. The MAC said in its appeal that the Big Ten should've used the embedded-clock feed used on the TV broadcast, in Saturday's case NBC and Peacock. The clocks weren't perfectly synced.

While the NCAA said it can't overturn a game outcome, and added that the Division I Football Bowl Subdivision Oversight Committee has no authority to overturn a game outcome, it did seem to side with the MAC's argument.

Available technology varies from conference to conference, creating a gray area when it comes to these situations. But according to The Athletic, the NCAA sent a memo to conferences Tuesday that clarified how the system should work moving forward. The memo states the embedded stadium clock on the TV feed should be used to determine if extra time should be added. In the memo, according to The Athletic, the NCAA said that if the TV feed doesn't have the embedded clock in use, then officials must use the game-clock graphic being used by the TV feed.

If that had been the case Saturday, Michigan wouldn't have been given one more second, and one more play — and Western Michigan would've walked away with the biggest win in program history.

Instead, Western Michigan, a 27.5-point underdog against Michigan, has had to settle for the moral victory, and has decided to take the high road in its response to the officials' decision. That has led to a lot of positive publicity for the school — including TV appearances on national sports shows and even CNN, exposure worth millions that the school couldn't otherwise afford. WMU head coach Lance Taylor, meanwhile, said Tuesday that his team is ready to move forward with its season — starting Saturday, Sept. 12, at home against Monmouth.

Western Michigan's profile has been raised significantly because of the controversy, with the Broncos even receiving Associated Press Top 25 votes. The Broncos, the defending MAC champions, are a formidable early contender to be the Group of Six's representative in the College Football Playoff. A huge game against Boise State, another Group of Six playoff contender, looms Saturday, Sept. 26, at Waldo Stadium in Kalamazoo.

A CFP appearance would be worth at least $4 million for the MAC and its 13 football-playing members.

The first CFP rankings will come out Tuesday, Nov. 3.

This article originally appeared on The Detroit News: NCAA can't overturn WMU-Michigan, but it clarifies timer protocols

title: Can Oklahoma's success on the road last year help in 2026?
description: The Oklahoma Sooners are hoping to use their experience and success on the road to help in matchup with Michigan.
fullText:
The last time the Oklahoma Sooners were on the road was Nov. 15, 2025. That's when the Sooners took a trip to Tuscaloosa, Alabama, and did what very few have done in the Tide's stadium: Win.

The Sooners forced three turnovers, on their way to a 23-21 win over No. 4 Alabama – which snapped the Tide's 17-game home win streak. The victory was on the tail end of a tough slate of road games that many thought would inevitably force Oklahoma out of the College Football Playoff conversation. Instead, Oklahoma rallied its way to a 10-win season and a playoff berth.

Of those 10 wins, Oklahoma won all four of its true road games against Temple, South Carolina, No. 14 Tennessee and No. 4 Alabama. Along with that, the Sooners held their opponents to a combined 1.7 yards per rush and produced multiple turnovers in each game.

Now, the Sooners are back on the road, and they're traveling to a place they've never been before: The Big House in Ann Arbor, Mich., for a tough nonconference matchup. Michigan Stadium holds 107,601 people, making it the largest in college football. But Venables believes what his group learned last year can be valuable come Saturday as No. 11 Oklahoma takes on Michigan.

"I think there's a certain level of confidence that comes from having done it and gone through it," he said of winning on the road. "And so in those moments when adversity happens, which they will, how to handle it. Again, I think that builds you, just having the right type of poise, type of mentality, the right type of leadership, will come from the experience that our guys gained a year ago."

Every year is a new year with a new group. But positively for the Sooners, this is the most player retention Venables has had since becoming the head coach at Oklahoma. In fact, all 11 of his defensive starters began their careers at OU. Conversely, he's brought back a veteran quarterback, top wide receiver, running backs and much of the offensive line.

Venables understands for Oklahoma to be successful this season, they're going to have to be good on the road. Oklahoma's away games this season include Michigan, Georgia, Mississippi State, Florida, Missouri, and the annual neutral-site game against Texas. All of these stadiums bring their own challenges and environments like cowbells, hedges and thousands of passionate fans. It's why this early test is so pivotal.

The Sooners' head coach knows many players are back, but has this particular group of Sooners learned how to handle adversity? How to communicate in a loud environment, and how to ultimately punch back when the other team makes a big play? What better way to find out than on the road in The Big House?

title: Bills to honor their northern fans by having 'O Canada' also performed at home opener against Lions
description: The Buffalo Bills are honoring their fans to the north by having the Canadian national anthem performed at their home opener next week, and amid rising cross-border tensions with the United States.  The team on Wednesday announced that the Toronto-based musical act Barenaked Ladies will perform “O Canada” before the Bills' prime-time game against the Detroit Lions on Sept. 17.  The game will be the first regular-season outing played at the Bills’ new $2.1 billion Highmark Stadium.
fullText:
ORCHARD PARK, N.Y. (AP) — The Buffalo Bills are honoring their fans to the north by having the Canadian national anthem performed at their home opener next week, and amid rising cross-border tensions with the United States.

The team on Wednesday announced that the Toronto-based musical act Barenaked Ladies will perform "O Canada" before the Bills' prime-time game against the Detroit Lions on Sept. 17. They'll be followed by Hawaiian-born actress and singer Auli'i Cravalho performing the "Star-Spangled Banner."

The game will be the first regular-season outing played at the Bills' new $2.1 billion Highmark Stadium. The team previously announced that U.S. pop band OneRepublic will perform during halftime.

The Bills' nod to Canada comes as the team continues seeking to build its fanbase across southern Ontario and Toronto, the nation's largest metropolitan center, which is located about a two-hour drive from Buffalo.

This isn't the first time the Bills have played both anthems during games at Orchard Park. The Bills under former owner Ralph Wilson once hosted an annual Canadian fan appreciation game, which was scheduled near Canadian Thanksgiving, which falls on the second Monday of October.

The games were discontinued about 20 years ago, and before the team played a series of annual regular-season games in Toronto over a six-year span, ending in 2013.

The NHL's Buffalo Sabres have had both the Canadian and American anthems performed before each game no matter the opponent in a tradition that began with their inception in 1970. The Bills and Sabres are now both owned by Terry Pegula.

title: Several OKC Thunder players go bowling together in team-bonding exercise
description: Several Oklahoma City Thunder players go bowling together in team-bonding exercise.
fullText:
Only a few weeks remain until training camps begin. But the Oklahoma City Thunder are looking to get ahead of the curve. Now that we're in the final stage of the mundane NBA offseason, the title contender is spending it together. After all, this is the last time for seven-plus months before they return to the rigorous lifestyle of the regular season.

Several Thunder players have spent the last handful of days together practicing and working out. The added time is in hopes of entering 2026-27 Opening Night and beyond with some sorta momentum and chemistry. Another way to achieve that goal? Team-bonding exercises.

When you're on an NBA team, you're around the same group of people for most of the year. The Thunder are building up some rapport from the jump. After an offseason filled with cost-cutting moves, the back end of their bench is filled with young and unproven players. To get them up to speed, they recently spent an evening bowling together.

Chet Holmgren, Cason Wallace, Jared McCain, Jaylin Williams, Aday Mara, Bennett Stirtz, Otega Oweh and Brooks Barnhizer all attended an OKC-run bowling session. The group of eight is mostly made up of players the Thunder will lean on in their championship ambitions this upcoming year.

Holmgren and Wallace are sure-fire starters. You can pencil in McCain and Williams as part of the rotation. The rest — Mara, Stirtz, Oweh and Barnhizer — will show what they're made of. The Thunder badly needs some of their youth to be developmental success stories. After all, it's the only way to ensure they remain deep amid their title window.

Good to see the Thunder do a team-bonding activity. Everybody else in the NBA does the same around this time of the year. As cheesy as it sounds, the synergy needs to extend beyond just the basketball court. For the last couple of years, OKC has had everybody on the same page. It hopes that it rolls over to this upcoming season.

title: Patriots fans confident in team’s direction, survey shows
description: Patriots fans see the team heading in the right direction.
fullText:
The New England Patriots took a major step forward in 2025.

After hiring Mike Vrabel as the team's head coach, the Patriots went from winning four games to 14 last season as Drake Maye established himself as one of the league's best quarterbacks.

New England's magical run ended sourly, however, as they dropped Super Bowl LX to the Seattle Seahawks. That led to a busy offseason in which they turned over a large portion of their roster, highlighted by the additions of A.J. Brown and Romeo Doubs at wide receiver.

Those offseason changes have the Patriots positioned to be competitive yet again as they hope to return to the Super Bowl and leave with a different outcome. Entering the 2026 season, New England is tied for the seventh-best odds on FanDuel Sportsbook to hoist the Lombardi Trophy, fifth-best in the AFC.

That is why in the results of the latest SB Nation Reacts survey, 96% of participants believe the Patriots continue to head in the right direction as a franchise.

The comment section was largely in agreement:

Looks at where this team was 18 months ago.

Yeah, I'd say they are heading in the right direction.

Glad to see this poll in 90s as it should be.

They are in a better place than they were a few years ago and possibly even better than last season…. Let's hope for the best…

I like what the FO has done the last 2 years. Doesn't mean they will hit on every move (and non-move) but the approach is solid. They have avoided huge overpays but they've been willing to do small overpays in strategic situations. And last year's draft class was excellent. That said, you can't address every need at once and we are tolerating some risks this year (ED unit is weak, OL is shallow, LBs lack speed).

I feel like we could be a year away from greatness if things bresk right. If we can solidify what we have this year we can hit the offseason with a reasonable to-do list.

All in all, this week's survey results look as follows:

Much of the recent optimism around the team stems from the Patriots agreeing on a long-term contract extension with cornerback Christian Gonzalez.

Gonzalez has become one of the league's best defensive players since the Patriots selected him in the first-round of the 2023 NFL Draft. The 24-year old was a key part of the team reaching the Super Bowl last season and is now under contract through the 2031 season following his $135 million extension.

The deal is the richest contract in team history, which fans supported as 61% of participants graded the extension an A. 23% went with a B while 11% voted a C to take up the majority of the voting.

In a recent report, journalist Pete O'Rourke offered an update on the future of Sunderland winger Chemsdine Talbi. It has been claimed that the Moroccan talent is close to leaving the Black Cats to join Al-Ittihad in the coming days.

Talbi played a useful role in the Wearside club's squad in the previous campaign as he managed to put in a run of productive displays for them in the Premier League. The 21-year-old scored four times and earned a couple of assists in 30 matches for Sunderland last season in various competitions.

His current contract at the Stadium of Light will run out in the summer of 2030. Hence, the Black Cats are under no immediate pressure to cash in on him.

SUNDERLAND, ENGLAND – SEPTEMBER 08: Chemsdine Talbi of Sunderland is challenged by Lewis Coyle of Hull City during the Carabao Cup Third Round match between Sunderland and Hull City at Stadium of Light on September 08, 2026 in Sunderland, England. (Photo by George Wood/Getty Images)

Talbi is a good dribbler with the ball at his feet and can make some driving runs with it out on the flanks. He has the vision to engineer some inviting chances in the final third and can shoot the ball with venom from long range.

The Moroccan sensation can even contribute by scoring and creating a few important goals for his side. Talbi is primarily a right-winger but can also operate as a left-sided wide player or play in the number ten position if asked to do so. However, he is not guaranteed a regular first-team spot at the Wearside club and could benefit from a change of scenery in search of more first-team starts in the future.

Hence, it is only fair to Talbi if the Black Cats allow him to leave this month. He would benefit from such a move, while Sunderland can trim their squad and make room for further additions to their squad next year.

At 21, Talbi has a bright future ahead of him as long as he continues to improve with each year. Therefore, his exit would be a good move for both the player and the Wearside club this month.

title: LSU president tells Greg Sankey school complied with SEC rules, calls dispute 'moot'
description: LSU president Wade Rousse called the SEC's legal dispute with the Tigers "moot" in a letter to Greg Sankey after LSU left former NFL players off its roster.
fullText:
LSU president Wade Rousse is calling for the SEC's legal dispute with the university to be deemed "moot" after the Tigers ultimately did not add any former NFL players to their 105-man roster.

In a letter obtained by USA TODAY Sports, the LSU president wrote to SEC commissioner Greg Sankey on Wednesday, Sept. 9 to "clear up allegations" against LSU. The letter confirms the Tigers would not add Dae'Quan Wright or Zxavian Harris to their roster, amid threats of punishment from the conference.

"On the afternoon of September 4, 2026, I called and provided you with advance notice that LSU would not place Dae'Quan Wright or Zxavian Harris on the football roster. This was confirmed when LSU submitted its roster that evening. On September 8, 2026, LSU filled its two remaining roster spots with eligible student-athletes. The roster is now locked for the season. LSU complied with SEC rules. This issue is moot," Rousse wrote.

REQUIRED READING: SEC vs. LSU hearing suddenly delayed. What happens next?

LSU confirmed to USA TODAY on Tuesday, Sept. 8 that the Tigers added Aiden Anding and Gabriel Reliford to their NCAA-mandated 105-man roster, leaving no available path for DaeQuan Wright or Zxavian Harris to join the roster later this season.

"That wasn't easy," LSU coach Lane Kiffin said on "College GameDay" on Saturday, Sept. 5 about why the Tigers didn't add Wright and Harris to their roster before Week 1 vs. Clemson. "... I had to make a decision that is for the big picture for LSU and the LSU football program, with the uncertainties of what potentially could have come by adding them to the roster."

Wright and Harris were attempting to return to college after signing with NFL teams over the offseason. Both players were seniors last season and joined NFL teams earlier this year before ultimately being waived, but after the NCAA implemented a five-for-five eligibility model, Wright and Harris were part of a lawsuit in Louisiana that ended with a judge granting a temporary restraining order that would have allowed them to play at the college level. Both players had committed to LSU and coach Lane Kiffin, who they had previously played for at Mississippi.

The SEC filed suit against LSU in the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Alabama on Thursday, Sept. 3, seeking preliminary and permanent injunctions tied to what it described as its First Amendment right of "expressive association" — in other words, the conference's argument that it cannot be forced to associate with a member acting contrary to its mission and values. That hearing was scheduled for Wednesday, Sept. 9, but was continued and will be rescheduled just before its scheduled start time.

Rousse's letter to Sankey also touched on the SEC's scheduled Thursday, Sept. 10 meeting, where presidents and chancellors are expected to consider LSU's status within the conference. It remains unclear if that vote will remain on the agenda.

Rousse also called that meeting's incentive to be "moot" as LSU won't "challenge, disrupt or seek to cancel or postpone" it.

LSU is scheduled to host Louisiana Tech at 7:30 p.m. ET on Saturday, Sept. 12 in Week 2.

USA TODAY reporters Craig Meyer and Matthew Glenesk and USA TODAY Network reporter Emilee Smarr contributed to this story

Be sure to check out USA TODAY Sports' new College Football Unfiltered podcast, hosted by USA TODAY Sports columnist Blake Toppmeyer. You can stream on YouTube or download via Apple podcasts and Spotify.
