title: Kudlow to Cruz: ‘You might want to think’ about announcing presidential bid in November
description: Fox Business host Larry Kudlow on Tuesday told Sen. Ted Cruz (R-Texas) that he “might want to think” about launching a bid for the presidency in November. Kudlow asked the Texas senator about whether ...
fullText:
Fox Business host Larry Kudlow on Tuesday told Sen. Ted Cruz (R-Texas) that he "might want to think" about launching a bid for the presidency in November.

Kudlow asked the Texas senator about whether or not he will run for the Republican nomination for president in 2028 in an appearance on the host's show.

"So, what I will say is there will be plenty of time to have that conversation after the midterms," Cruz answered. "We're less than 60 days out from the midterms, so my focus –– if we lose the House and Senate, all the legislative progress we have grinds to a halt, and it is two years of warfare against President Trump and his agenda."

Kudlow noted how Trump declared his candidacy right after the 2022 midterms and credited that to his success in 2024.

"I'm just putting it out there," he said. "You might want to think about it. I mean, right after he did that, a lot of people scratched their heads, and it turns out that was a close outbid. It really was."

Cruz previously ran for president in 2016 and at one point was seen as a front-runner. He won 11 state contests, including the Iowa caucuses, before suspending his campaign as Trump built a large delegate lead.

The Texan eventually backed President Trump in the general election, though he did not endorse him at the GOP's convention in Cleveland that summer, and was then booed by Trump supporters.

At the time, Cruz reportedly told allies that he thought there was something "fundamentally wrong" with evangelical voters backing Trump. Then-candidate Trump threatened to "spill the beans" on Cruz's wife, Heidi Cruz, and reposted an unflattering photo of her compared with one of first lady Melania Trump, and he claimed there was "voter fraud" in his loss to Cruz in Iowa.

The Texas senator is seen as a Republican contender for president in 2028 and has said the GOP has not coalesced around Vice President Vance as the party's presidential nominee.

"There's going to be a full discussion about who we are and what we believe," Cruz told MS NOW's Ali Vitali late last month when asked if the party has settled on Vance.

Cruz added that the GOP was in "the midst of a debate about who our party is," noting that there will be "time to figure" out his role in that future.

Vance and Secretary of State Marco Rubio, who ran against Cruz and Trump in 2016, are seen as favorites to possibly succeed Trump. Neither has said publicly whether they will run in 2028, but both of their names are mentioned as potential GOP contenders.

A recent Emerson College poll showed Rubio outperforming Vance in multiple hypothetical 2028 presidential match-ups against Democratic candidates.

title: Trump administration proposes dropping huge swath of immigrants from US census
description: The Trump administration proposed on Wednesday changing the national census to include only U.S. citizens and permanent residents, a move that could significantly
fullText:
Sept 9 (Reuters) - The Trump administration proposed on Wednesday changing the national census to include only U.S. citizens and permanent residents, a move that could significantly change how much ‌political representation and federal funding each state receives.

The U.S. Census Bureau submitted the proposal just over ‌a year after President Donald Trump ordered its parent agency to craft a new census that would block immigrants in the U.S. ​illegally from being counted. The bureau will conduct the next full census in 2030.

The proposed rule changes would exclude even more immigrants from the census, such as those in the U.S. on a temporary lawful basis. The proposed changes would also eliminate parts of the questionnaire that seek information on race or ethnicity, which have been included ‌since the first census in 1790.

The proposal ⁠is open to public comment for 30 days.

Demography experts and civil rights advocates warn that both changes could warp the data used for drawing congressional and state legislative ⁠districts, enforcing anti-discrimination law and allocating federal funds for public services.

FEDERAL AID, POLITICAL REPRESENTATION AT STAKE

The effort could have "earth-shattering" effects, leaving cities and states that have relatively high immigrant populations with insufficient federal aid and political representation, said Meeta Anand, ​senior ​director of the census and data equity program at the ​Leadership Conference on Civil and Human Rights.

Census ‌data "undergirds so much of our democracy and our society," Anand said. "So you'll start seeing a very inaccurate picture of our country, and then we're making political decisions, business decisions, investment decisions based on data that are flawed."

The White House did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Trump has long decried the fact that immigrants living in the U.S. illegally are included in the census, which is used to determine how many seats each ‌state gets in the U.S. House of Representatives and state ​legislative districts.

In his first term, Trump tried to add a citizenship ​question to the 2020 census but was blocked ​by the U.S. Supreme Court, which ruled that the federal government had given a "contrived" rationale.

The ‌U.S. Constitution's 14th Amendment calls for political representatives ​to be apportioned based on "the ​whole number of persons in each State."

The administration's effort to omit immigrants in the U.S. illegally and temporary immigrants from the U.S. census comes amid its wider crackdown on both legal and illegal ​immigration across the country.

The Justice Department ‌warned on September 2 that states could lose billions of dollars in welfare funding if they do ​not report all immigrants whom state agencies know to be in the country illegally.

title: Why Conservative Republicans Are Worried About License Plate Cameras
description: Recent comments by Greg Abbott and Ron DeSantis reflect a bipartisan backlash against warrantless surveillance.
fullText:
Last month, Texas Gov. Greg Abbott froze state funding for automated license plate readers (ALPRs), acknowledging concerns about the warrantless surveillance enabled by such AI-assisted cameras. Abbott took that step the day after Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis, a fellow Republican, declared that ALPRs are "out of control."

Both governors cited recent reports about police officers accused of using ALPR data for personal purposes, which seem to be driving a shift in public opinion about the technology. Such incidents highlight the perils of giving cops across the country easy access to such data, which they can use to track your travels, identify nearby vehicles, and even predict your itinerary, without judicial oversight or meaningful internal supervision.

Abbott mentioned a Lufkin, Texas, police officer who was charged with using ALPR information to stalk an ex-girlfriend, her relatives, and her acquaintances more than 10,000 times. DeSantis alluded to similar cases in Florida, where officers in Sarasota and Haines City had recently been arrested for misusing ALPR data.

"When I see, like, a police officer using this to track, like, an ex-girlfriend," DeSantis said, "I'm like, you know, what the hell's going on?" Local officials are beginning to ask the same question.

As of Tuesday, the Institute for Justice counted 181 local governments that have canceled or declined to renew ALPR contracts since the beginning of 2025. In Texas alone, The Dallas Express reports, at least 23 jurisdictions have dropped contracts, suspended service, or reduced the size of their ALPR networks.

Some 7,000 police departments have installed those networks, which include around 140,000 cameras, without giving much thought to the privacy implications or the potential for abuse. But some of them are now having second thoughts, reflecting rising public skepticism of unconstrained ALPR use.

In a YouGov survey last month, 46 percent of respondents opposed police use of ALPRs, including 31 percent who were "strongly" opposed, while 38 percent favored the practice. A year ago, by contrast, YouGov found that 45 percent of Americans supported ALPRs, while 33 percent opposed them, including 20 percent who were "strongly" opposed.

That reversal coincides with proliferating reports of blatant ALPR abuses. The Institute for Justice has identified "well over 100" such incidents, which it notes "may be just the tip of the iceberg" given the reality of lax oversight and widespread data sharing.

Police officers are supposed to use that information, which they can access on computers or mobile phones, only for legitimate law enforcement purposes. But as a Wichita police supervisor conceded in 2024, it's "not even possible" to enforce that policy by making sure that each search complies with it.

Compounding that challenge, each agency typically shares ALPR information with many others. Once that happens, The Wichita Eagle noted in 2022, local police officials have "no control over how those outside agencies use it and no way to flag unlawful searches."

In Norfolk, Virginia, a local radio station reported last April, police officers often give "incomplete and imprecise reasons" for ALPR searches, including "suspect," "suspicious," and "investigation" or "inv." Such vague labels hardly seem consistent with a state law requiring that cops state a "specific purpose," including "the offense type," thereby providing enough information to determine whether a search is legitimate.

"The police cannot police themselves," says Institute for Justice attorney Robert Frommer. His organization argues that a warrant generally should be required to access ALPR data—a policy it aims to establish by challenging ALPR networks on Fourth Amendment grounds and urging states to enact protective legislation.

The congressional response to ALPRs, including several bills and an investigation that Sen. Josh Hawley (R–Mo.) announced last month, has been dominated by conservative Republicans, which confirms that the backlash is not limited to libertarian or left-leaning critics. Whether it will yield effective constraints is another question.

ALPRs are "easily containable," Abbott says, a bit overoptimistically. "They're going to be required to be used responsibly if they're used at all."

The post Why Conservative Republicans Are Worried About License Plate Cameras appeared first on Reason Magazine.

title: 'How many times do I have to say no?!': Pirro dodges Reflecting Pool case questions
description: Pirro interrupted reporters as soon as they mentioned Hearn's case.
fullText:
D.C. U.S. Attorney Jeanine Pirro vented frustration at reporters on Wednesday as she repeatedly refused to answer questions about a topic that has landed her in hot water with President Donald Trump: his demands that she revisit the now-dismissed Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool vandalism case against former Olympian David Hearn.

In a news conference involving an unrelated crackdown targeting Chinese scam centers, Pirro interrupted reporters in at least three exchanges as soon as they mentioned Hearn's case.

Asked by ABC News if she plans to revisit the Reflecting Pool case against Hearn per Trump's request, Pirro interrupted: "Ah -- why did I know that was coming?"

"President Trump has made clear that this is very important to him," ABC News responded.

"And you know the president has the right to decide what he wants to do and what is important," Pirro replied.

Judge indicates Trump's pressure campaign could permanently sink Reflecting Pool vandalism case

When another reporter later followed up and attempted to ask about Hearn's case, Pirro again interrupted, "No, I'm not going there! Don't even go there."

At one point, after a reporter made another final attempt, Pirro yelled, "No! No and no! .... How many times do I have to say no?!"

Olympian David Hearn indicted for alleged vandalism of Reflecting Pool

Pirro's news conference is the first since her surprise move to dismiss the felony indictment against Hearn in August. In a filing, Pirro admitted that damage to the Reflecting Pool was likely caused by "botched" installation and not by vandals.

The move prompted outrage from Trump who said Pirro "choked" in her handling of the case, and later refused to rule out firing Pirro who he urged to "re-visit" the decision to charge Hearn.

"U.S. Attorney Jeanine Pirro should re-visit her hastily made decision [to dismiss Hearn's indictment]," Trump wrote in an Aug. 7 post on social media.

The judge who previously oversaw Hearn's case is currently weighing whether to dismiss the case "with prejudice," which would effectively bar prosecutors from seeking another indictment against Hearn.

Hearn's attorneys have said that Trump is still pushing a "false version" of the events around the Reflecting Pool, bolstering their argument that the government should be blocked from pursuing charges again.

title: Brazil court crisis deepens as justice orders federal police chief suspended
description: Brazil's Supreme Court crisis deepened on Tuesday as Justice Andre Mendonca ordered the suspension of federal police
fullText:
RIO DE JANEIRO/BRASILIA, Sept 8 (Reuters) - Brazil's escalating Supreme Court crisis deepened on Tuesday as Justice Andre Mendonca ordered the suspension of federal police chief Andrei Rodrigues, a ‌decision backed by the majority of a five-member court panel but likely to be challenged by the government.

The ‌move marks a dramatic new chapter in an unprecedented conflict that has engulfed Brazil's top court, pitting Mendonca against fellow Justice Alexandre de Moraes, and ​comes as the country heads into a tight presidential election next month.

Moraes is one of Brazil's most powerful and divisive figures, whose aggressive pursuit of former President Jair Bolsonaro and his allies over a 2023 coup plot led to Bolsonaro's conviction last year.

Right-wing opposition leaders have sought to tie leftist President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva to Moraes, while using the court crisis to ‌bolster the presidential campaign of Senator Flavio ⁠Bolsonaro, the former president's eldest son.

Recent polls suggested Lula and Flavio Bolsonaro are running neck and neck. Thousands of opposition supporters took to the streets on Independence Day on Monday to protest ⁠against Lula and Moraes and voice support for Mendonca, a Bolsonaro appointee.

Mendonca last week disclosed a report raising questions about alleged contacts between Moraes and a banker accused of leading a multibillion-dollar fraud scheme, prompting calls for an investigation of the justice.

Moraes responded ​by seeking ​an investigation into Mendonca for alleged abuse of authority, citing federal ​police intelligence reports that Mendonca has now challenged ‌as illegal.

Mendonca ordered the preventive suspension of Rodrigues, the director-general of the Federal Police, and Leandro Almada, the agency's intelligence chief, over their alleged involvement in the production of the intelligence reports.

The Federal Police did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

A majority of the five-member Supreme Court panel reviewing the case backed Mendonca's decision, with Justices Kassio Nunes Marques, another Bolsonaro appointee, and Luiz Fux joining him.

A top Lula aide, nevertheless, slammed Mendonca's move as unwarranted judicial overreach.

"Investigating possible evidence ‌of crimes is correct. But this measure smells electoral to me. That ​cannot happen," Institutional Relations Minister Jose Guimaraes said on social media.

A source familiar with the matter said Lula's ​government was expected to appeal the decision as early as Tuesday.

The solicitor general's office is expected ‌to argue that suspending the federal police chief violates ​powers constitutionally reserved to the ​president, the source said.

In the ruling seen by Reuters, Mendonca said the measure was necessary to preserve the independence of the judiciary and ensure that justices, the solicitor general and police officials could perform their duties free ​from "illegal constraints."

He said that the "exceptional gravity and ‌illegality" surrounding the intelligence reports allegedly involving Rodrigues required immediate action as judicial and police functions risked continuing ​to be "vilified."

title: Brennan sprints to historic fifth stage win at Vuelta
description: Great Britain's Matthew Brennan continues his remarkable Grand Tour debut by sprinting to a fifth stage victory of this year's Vuelta a Espana in Seville.
fullText:
Great Britain's Matthew Brennan continued his remarkable Grand Tour debut by sprinting to a fifth stage victory at this year's Vuelta a Espana.

The 21-year-old Visma Lease-a-bike rider edged out Jordi Meeus and Magnus Cort in a bunch sprint to win the 17th stage of the Grand Tour in Seville.

In doing so, Brennan became the youngest-ever rider to reach five Grand Tour victories.

Just like he did after winning stage 16 on Tuesday, the Briton raised his hands in the air as he crossed the finish line but this time with five fingers up to mark his fifth stage win of the race.

The largely flat 185km route from Dos Hermanas to Seville was always expected to favour the sprinters.

Spain's Sinuhe Fernandez and France's Enzo Paleni broke away early and created a gap of more than five minutes on the peloton at the halfway point.

Groupama FDJ-United rider Paleni then dropped Fernandez but was caught by the peloton with just three kilometres remaining.

Brennan came around Cort in the closing metres before holding off Meeus to seal another impressive victory in a dramatic finish.

In the general classification, Spain's Enric Mas, eyeing a first Grand Tour victory, maintained his lead over Felix Gall, with four-time Vuelta winner Primoz Roglic in third place.

Stage 18 on Thursday is a 32.1km individual time trial, offering one of the last opportunities for Mas' rivals to reduce their gap to the leader.

title: 'Just a number' - Rybakina's rise to world number one
description: Elena Rybakina becomes the new women's world number one after reaching the US Open semi-finals, ending Aryna Sabalenka's 99-week reign at the top of the rankings.
fullText:
After 99 weeks, there will be a new women's world number one - and it will be Elena Rybakina.

Rybakina confirmed she will replace Aryna Sabalenka at the top of the world rankings on Monday with her US Open quarter-final victory over China's Zheng Qinwen.

Despite losing a set for the first time in the tournament, Rybakina fought back and saved a break point in the deciding set to complete a 3-6 6-1 6-4 win.

She is the first Kazakhstani man or woman to reach the top of the singles standings.

Rybakina has been in hot pursuit of Sabalenka this season and arrived in New York as one of three women who threatened the Belarusian's position, alongside Americans Jessica Pegula and Coco Gauff.

However, the other three contenders each needed to win the title and hope Rybakina exited before the semi-finals to capture the number one spot.

Sabalenka's consecutive 99-week reign as world number one stretches back to 21 October 2024 and stands as the sixth-longest streak in WTA history.

The top two players could yet meet in the US Open final - just as they did at this year's Australian Open, where Rybakina prevailed in three sets.

For Rybakina, the trophy is more important than her new ranking.

"It's just a number right now. My goal is to win the tournaments which I play," the 27-year-old sad.

"It's an amazing achievement, but you know how quickly everything can change in tennis ranking-wise."

Rybakina will face either Coco Gauff or Mirra Andreeva in Thursday's semi-finals, while Sabalenka takes on Jessica Pegula.

Shelton beats Alcaraz in late-night 'war' to reach semis

Rybakina's push for the world number one ranking started at the end of 2025.

After losing to Sabalenka in the quarter-finals of the Wuhan Open last October, Rybakina clinched the Ningbo Open title one week later before taking her revenge by beating Sabalenka to win the season-ending WTA Finals.

She carried that momentum into 2026, getting the better of Sabalenka again but this time in a major final. She beat her fellow big-server in three competitive sets to win the Australian Open - her second Slam title almost four years after her first at Wimbledon.

Since then, Sabalenka has come out on top in their Indian Wells final and Miami Open semi-final, but Rybakina took the Stuttgart title on clay as Sabalenka's form fluctuated.

After disappointing early exits at the French Open and Wimbledon, she reached the final in Toronto, losing in straight sets to Iga Swiatek.

Rybakina's bid to replace Sabalenka suffered another setback when she was forced to retire injured from her Cincinnati Open quarter-final against Swiatek last month.

Rybakina later revealed that the left ankle problem, which hindered her movement and prevented her pushing off properly when serving, had been "bothering me for a long period of time" but was something she felt she had "under control".

Speaking before the US Open, Rybakina admitted her preparation "wasn't great" as she was unable to train for much of the week leading into the tournament.

However, that has not stopped her from achieving the first of her two major goals in New York.

Rybakina's rise to world number one has coincided with one of the most consistent periods of her career.

Despite managing her ankle injury in the lead-up to the US Open, Rybakina has backed up a 78-match 2025 season by playing 60 times so far this year.

She has won 47 of those matches, a tally bettered only by American world number three Pegula (50) on the WTA Tour.

Only Pegula can match her tally of 34 wins on hard courts this season.

But Rybakina has also won the majority of her matches against the tour's other leading players, winning 13 of her 20 meetings with fellow top-20 players.

Undoubtedly Rybakina's biggest weapon is her powerful serve.

She has recorded the most aces on the WTA Tour this year, with her total standing at 394 in 2026.

Rybakina's serve was at its devastating best against Naomi Osaka in the fourth round - she won 87% of her first-serve points and fired in seven aces among her 29 winners, but limited her unforced errors to 17.

Speaking after the match, Osaka said: "The immediate thought that I had in my head when she hit the ace, I was, like, 'well, I can't really do anything about it'."

"Maybe I could have covered it, but she has a great serve, so she probably would have hit the other way."

Rybakina has worked with coach Stefano Vukov for almost seven years.

The pair first worked together from 2019 to 2025 before splitting. Later that year Vukov was banned from the WTA Tour for breaching its code of conduct, following an independent investigation into his behaviour towards Rybakina.

Vukov, who has coached Rybakina since she was a teenager, denied any wrongdoing, and Rybakina said she was never mistreated by him.

Rybakina sought his return to her team at the start of 2025. The Croat successfully appealed the suspension and began working with Rybakina again in August last year.

She reached the US Open fourth round for the first time in her career at her first tournament since reuniting with Vukov, before embarking on the strong end-of-season form which has now propelled her to the pinnacle of the sport.

title: England demolish Pakistan to take charge of Test
description: England again demolish the dismal Pakistan batting to move on course for a 3-0 clean sweep on the opening day of the third Test at Edgbaston.
fullText:
Third Rothesay Test, Edgbaston (day one of five)

Pakistan 133: Shakeel 43; Tongue 4-42, Robinson 3-15, Archer 3-25

England 156-4: Gay 60, Brook 52*

England again demolished the dismal Pakistan batting to move on course for a 3-0 clean sweep on the opening day of the third Test at Edgbaston.

After ripping out the tourists for only 133, England already have a 23-run advantage on 156-4.

Following a week of turmoil in which Pakistan sent seven players home, called up seven more and changed their coach, the outcome was much the same as the first two Tests.

Though the dry pitch seemed good for batting, a moody morning sky convinced England captain Joe Root to field first and his new-look pace attack was outstanding once more.

Pakistan failed to reach 200 for the fifth consecutive innings, while none of the top five made double figures. Saud Shakeel at least managed 43 and the ineptitude of the top order was put into context by last-wicket pair Muhammad Abbas and Mohammad Ali adding 26 in 46 balls - the best partnership of the innings.

Josh Tongue bowled quickly for his 4-42, Ollie Robinson passed 100 Test wickets with his 3-15 and Jofra Archer claimed the remaining three scalps.

In truth, it was a disappointing and dispiriting spectacle, but Pakistan showed some fight with the ball, not least when rapid debutant Razaullah inflicted yet another lbw on Root to leave England 39-3.

Emilio Gay and Harry Brook steadied England, each making half-centuries in a stand of 104 that pushed the hosts into the lead.

Gay dragged on off Razaullah. His gritty 60 was impressive, if perhaps not enough to provide certainty around his place in a congested England batting line-up.

Gay should open for England in South Africa - Cook

England lead 'embarrassing' Pakistan

The pattern of this day was entirely predictable from the moment Root won the toss and there were times in the early going when the action was neither elite sport nor satisfying entertainment.

The conditions for a Test played in September were autumnal and one side of Edgbaston is a building site. Some 15,000 tickets were sold for today, yet the ground was not half-full when play began. The atmosphere was flat.

Pakistan made four changes from the second Test at Lord's, including three debutants. England, as expected, resisted tinkering with their attack and the hosts had the Pakistan innings wrapped up in 33.5 overs.

At least Pakistan landed some blows on the England top-order. Ben Duckett and Jordan Cox played loose shots - potentially costly for Cox as he looks to nail down his place - and Root was lbw for the 10th time in 13 innings in Razaullah's first over in Test cricket.

Gay and Brook restored order in the evening sunshine and it already seems certain England will win before the weekend. It could even be over inside two days.

Quite what Root's developing England team can take from this series is unclear. The disparity between the two sides in these conditions is simply too large.

Gay has had the entire summer to make the opening position his own, though the arrivals of Cox and Dan Lawrence could make him most vulnerable when Jacob Bethell returns from a knee injury.

But Gay has been batting in the hardest position at a time when all batters have struggled for runs. This knock, in an innings when Cox wasted his chance, did his cause no harm without being a compelling case for long-term retention.

The Durham man was patient and watchful and also came through moments of frantic running with Brook. When the opportunity arose, the left-hander scored with handsome strokes through the off side.

Brook arrived when Razaullah was pushing the speed gun, and the England vice-captain also had to battle his recent weakness with the wicketkeeper standing up.

The fourth-wicket pair gradually halted Pakistan's brief spell of momentum, taking England ahead.

For Gay, a third half-century in six Tests came from 95 deliveries. Reaching the close unbeaten would have presented a golden opportunity for a big score on Thursday, only for a limp prod at Razaullah to leave more questions and a sense of what might have been.

Robinson began this summer in an exile from the England team that had lasted for more than two years. He ends it as the attack leader, with statistics that stack up alongside some of the all-time greats of the game.

He had already had one lbw decision against Saim Ayub overturned by the time he pinned the same batter again in his second over. It gave Robinson his 100th Test wicket at an average of 19.34 - the first England bowler since Ian Botham to reach 100 wickets at an average below 20.

Indeed, no bowler since World War II with at least 100 Test wickets has a better average than Robinson. His three on Wednesday gave him a total of 27 for the summer at a cost of 7.96 apiece.

Such was their dominance, England could afford Duckett to miss two tough chances at first slip. Root, often captaining from short leg, set fields that crowded the bat, often with seven catchers.

Tongue bowled with high pace and targeted the stumps – all four of his wickets were bowled or lbw. Archer benefitted from two miscues from mid-on, then came back to eventually end the Ali-Abbas last-wicket stand.

The curiosity is Gus Atkinson. He has not bowled badly, yet has somehow missed out on the riches of his fellow seamers. While the rest have cleaned up, Atkinson has just one wicket in the series at an average of 156.

'Embarrassing' Pakistan break record in innings to forget

Pakistan investigate 'discipline and conduct'

title: Andoni Iraola has already made his decision on future of ‘strong’ defender
description: Andoni Iraola made a fair few changes to Liverpool's squad during the summer transfer window. The Spaniard welcomed four new players through the Anfield doors and, although this is a decent number of ...
fullText:
Andoni Iraola made a fair few changes to Liverpool's squad during the summer transfer window.

The Spaniard welcomed four new players through the Anfield doors and, although this is a decent number of signings, it still feels like the Reds could've done with bringing more in.

There are still a couple of gaping holes among their first-team squad that could do with filling but for now, the former Bournemouth boss needs to make do with what he's got at his disposal.

Before the next transfer window comes around, it does feel like some decisions will need to be made on the future of some Liverpool players.

Some, such as Luke Chambers are already being linked with a move away but, looking even further ahead at the 2027 summer transfer window, it's clear that more money will need to be spent.

So, the fact that Iraola already seems to be making decisions on the future of some players proves that he's the right man for the job, especially if the Reds are wanting to get back to their best.

Even though two new defenders were added to Liverpool's ranks this summer, it still feels like more could be done to improve their back line.

Ronald Araujo is only on a season-long loan and, while he does have an option to buy included in the deal, it's still unclear whether the Reds will activate it or not.

Virgil van Dijk's contract is also set to expire at the end of the current season and, even though most fans want him to stay, no rumours of negotiations have started to emerge yet.

So, the fact that Fussball News have shared that Atletico Madrid's Marc Pubill is on Liverpool's shortlist makes a lot of sense.

"According to information from fussball-news.de, Arsenal, Manchester United, Chelsea, and Liverpool are among the interested parties. While no concrete negotiations are currently underway, the English clubs are keeping a close eye on Pubill," they wrote.

"A transfer is unlikely to be easy or cheap for Premier League clubs. Pubill is under contract with Atlético until June 30, 2030. This gives the Madrid club considerable negotiating power.

"According to information from fussball-news.de, Atlético sees the defender as an important part of its future plans. Should the club even consider talks about a sale, any interested party would have to dig deep into their pockets.

"A transfer fee of between 55 and 60 million euros is currently being discussed as a possible starting point for negotiations. Performance-related bonuses and other contract terms could also play a role."

Araujo and Pubill both play in the exact same positions.

Each of them can be used as a centre-back or a right-back but, the fact that Pubill is around five years younger than the Uruguayan proves why he'd be a smarter investment for Liverpool.

Indeed, if Van Dijk and Alisson both exit L4 next summer, there would be a major lack of leadership around Anfield so, in that case, Araujo would probably be a smart signing.

However, with how extensively Liverpool have planned their transfers for the future, the fact that Pubill could grow to become an even better player than he already is will be a major selling point for the Anfield outfit.

In a way, they could both technically join Liverpool next term but, with Pubill being priced the same as Araujo, signing the younger of the two makes a lot more sense.

title: Liam Coen with Week 1 injury updates on Cole Van Lanen, LeQuint Allen
description: Ahead of the Jaguars' Week 1 game with the Browns, Liam Coen provided injury updates on Cole Van Lanen and LeQuint Allen.
fullText:
The Jacksonville Jaguars are back on the practice field on Wednesday in preparation for their season-opener against the Cleveland Browns.

Entering the week, the statuses of Cole Van Lanen and LeQuint Allen remain up in the air at this time. Van Lanen is still ramping up from a knee injury that sidelined him late last season, while Allen suffered a soft tissue injury on Aug. 17 and has been out since.

Both will be game-time decisions on Sunday.

"I think he'll be a game-time decision," Coen said of Van Lanen. "I would imagine working him out before the game and seeing what that's going to look like. Just using every op we can to get him to potentially be ready to go. We'll kind of take it all the way up to game time with that one."

With Anton Harrison spending much of training camp at left tackle with Van Lanen out, once Van Lanen does return, he will take over at right tackle. In his absence, Walker Little has been filling in.

"Yeah, you want to get him in," Coen added. "You want to be able to get him some work, get him some reps, get him feeling confident in a game-like setting. Missing the joints and all the other ops that our other guys obviously had throughout training camp, but I've really liked his mindset, I've like the way he's attacked putting himself in precarious positions and owning it. I think he's been very intentional about that and has been fearless with putting himself in some of the positions that he has throughout the course of practice. So I've really appreciated that and we'll see what it looks like on Sunday."

Allen often filled a third-down role as a rookie, excelling in pass protection from the running back position. This season, those responsibilities will continue to be on his plate, but he could see more opportunities in the pass game as well.

If Allen can't go on Sunday, Ameer Abdullah will be the Jaguars' third running back behind Bhayshul Tuten and Chris Rodriguez.

"Yeah, he'll be exactly very similar to Cole that way, where we'll work him out, we'll get a game-time decision from him," said Coen. "It's been a while, so we'll have to work through it, but I have a lot of faith in LeQuint and trust in him to be able to know the game plan and give us a chance if he's ready to go in that workout. I'll feel confident that he can come in and help our team."

This article originally appeared on Jaguars Wire: Liam Coen with Week 1 injury updates on Cole Van Lanen, LeQuint Allen

title: DE Micah Parsons could return before Packers-Cowboys game
description: Green Bay Packers pass rusher Micah Parsons is making progress in his return from knee surgery.
fullText:
The Green Bay Packers will begin the season without one of their key defensive players as Micah Parsons continues his recovery from reconstructive knee surgery. The Packers placed the edge rusher on the reserve/physically unable to perform list before the regular season, ruling him out for at least the first four games.

Parsons injured his left knee in Week 15 of the 2025 season against the Denver Broncos. He later underwent ACL surgery, which also included a meniscus procedure. The Packers have maintained a cautious approach throughout his rehabilitation.

The 27-year-old said during training camp that Week 6 was his most optimistic target for a return to game action. Green Bay general manager Brian Gutekunst also said last week that the team expected Parsons to be close once he completed the required four-game absence.

MORE: 49ers lose top player for the rest of the season

Green Bay Packers defensive end Micah Parsons (1) Mandatory Credit: Jeff Hanisch-Imagn Images)

There is optimism that Parsons could return in Week 5 when the Packers host the Chicago Bears, NFL insider Tom Pelissero reported Wednesday. If that does not happen, Week 6 against the Dallas Cowboys remains a realistic target.

The Packers face the Bears at Lambeau Field on Oct. 11 before hosting Dallas on Oct. 18. Parsons spent his first four NFL seasons with the Cowboys before Green Bay acquired him in a 2025 trade.

A Week 6 return would put Parsons back on the field against his former team. The matchup is set to be one of the more closely watched games on Green Bay's early schedule.

Parsons recorded 12.5 sacks, 19 tackles for the Packers last season before his injury. He earned his fourth career All-Pro selection.

His return timeline will depend on his recovery and clearance from the Packers' medical staff.

fullText:
Michigan news: Whittingham's quotes on Carr could hint at Underwood benching appeared first on ClutchPoints. 

The entire college football world has been focused on the Michigan clock scandal in their victory over Western Michigan. Michigan would not have been in the situation to need a Hail Mary to win the game had Bryce Underwood played better. This has led to the possibility that Underwood could be benched by Michigan.

Now, comments about the backup quarterback Tommy Carr, made by Kyle Whittingham in the spring, are being looked at and could be hinting at a potential benching of Underwood, per Matt Hayes of USA Today.

"He's just got 'it.' You watch him play, and it's so obvious," Whittingham said in the spring about Carr. "He's young, he's a freshman. But he's a ball player."

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Putting that in contrast with what Whittingham just said about Carr, there is a clear possibility that Underwood could be heading to the bench.

"He's our QB now," Whittingham said Monday of Underwood. "At some point, we've got to turn a corner and we've got to see improvement."

The Michigan offense was a disaster against Western Michigan. On the first drive of the game, Michigan drove the field and scored a touchdown. On the drive, Underwood completed all six passes he attempted for 57 yards. He also ran for 11 yards and a touchdown. On the final drive, he was two for six for 75 yards and a touchdown. In between, he was just four for ten, passing for 38 yards with an interception.

Michigan dropped out of the Top 25 after the win over Western Michigan, and if Underwood does not play better, they will not be returning. Michigan hosts Oklahoma on Saturday.

title: Rams vs. 49ers travel plans: How NFC West rivals have taken different approach to NFL Australia game
description: The Rams are taking a risk with their travel plans for their season-opener against the 49ers in Australia.
fullText:
Rams vs. 49ers travel plans: How NFC West rivals have taken different approach to NFL Australia game originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

When the NFL announced it was headed to Australia for the first time ever, the first question on many fans' minds was, "How's that going to work?"

As it turns out, the time zone disparity is barely an issue. While the NFL's London games are played in the morning back in the eastern time zone, the difference between U.S. time zones and the time in Melbourne is so massive that the game between the Rams and 49ers can actually air in primetime back in the United States.

The travel logistics are a different story. A 15-hour flight is something that can't be worked around, and each team is taking a vastly different approach to their travel plans before the key NFC West showdown.

Here's what you need to know about the travel plans for the Rams and 49ers before their game in Australia.

NFL Week 1 picks against the spread

The 49ers are taking a fairly traditional approach to international travel before an NFL game, as they flew to Australia on the night of Sept. 2, landing on the morning of Sept. 4 local time. That gave San Francisco a full week to adjust to the vastly different time zone, and it allowed the 49ers to run practices in Australia before playing on the morning of Sept. 11 — or the night of Sept. 10 by U.S. time zones.

The Rams are approaching their travel plans much differently. L.A. left Tuesday night on a 15-hour flight to land Thursday morning local time for a game that will be played on Friday morning in Melbourne. That makes Wednesday a "lost day" entirely and gives the Rams only about 27 hours from the moment they land in Melbourne to kickoff.

The 49ers' logic is understandable. Kyle Shanahan wants his team to have as much time as possible to adjust to the time difference and the new environment so it doesn't have a noticeable impact on gameday. Teams that play in Europe often head over earlier than they would for a typical stateside game to allow players to get acclimated.

The Rams have their reasons, too. "We felt like staying in our rhythm and routine," Sean McVay told the Orange County Register, explaining that every detail is "geared towards what we think is best for the players."

The decision is aimed at eliminating the need for players to acclimate at all. Teams don't typically play games in the morning, so by landing in Australia so soon before the game, the Rams are hoping to keep their players' body clocks geared toward where they would be later in the day.

The Rams, however, might nearly spend more time in the air than actually on the ground in Australia. They plan to head back to Los Angeles directly after the game, so it will be in-and-out of the country, as opposed to the 49ers, who are spending a week in Melbourne.

2026 NFL POSITIONAL RANKINGS: QBs | RBs | WRs | TEs | Defense

The 49ers arrived in Australia in the early morning hours of Sept. 4 local time, or on the afternoon of Sept. 3 in most U.S. time zones. That's almost exactly a week before kickoff, which gave San Francisco's players time to adjust to the significant time difference.

San Francisco and Melbourne are just under 8,000 miles apart, making it a long journey to Australia's southern coast.

It took 15 hours and six minutes for the 49ers to fly from San Francisco to Melbourne. Unfortunately, there is just no way around an arduous journey to Australia, even for NFL teams on the west coast. The 49ers tried to get ahead of that by flying out a week early.

Melbourne is 17 hours ahead of San Francisco. That means what will be a 5:35 p.m. kickoff on Thursday, Sept. 10 for fans on the American west coast will actually be a 10:35 a.m. kickoff on Friday, Sept. 11 in Melbourne.

MORE:Why the Bills are SN's pick to win Super Bowl 61

Los Angeles is also just under 8,000 miles away from Melbourne.

The flight from Los Angeles to Melbourne comes in at just under 15 hours, similar to the 15-hour, six-minute journey the 49ers had. There is no real difference in travel time for the Rams and 49ers, but because L.A. arranged its plans so differently than San Francisco, the game will be viewed partly as a battle of logistics.

Like San Francisco, Los Angeles is 17 hours behind Melbourne. A 5:35 p.m. kickoff on Thursday, Sept. 10 for fans on the American west coast will actually be a 10:35 a.m. kickoff on Friday, Sept. 11 in Melbourne.

title: Fantasy Football QB rankings in Week 1
description: The top QBs in Fantasy Football week one!
fullText:
Another NFL season is upon us, and the journey begins on Wednesday, not Thursday. We have an international game Down Under between the Rams and the 49ers. While the sport stays the same, there are so many new wrinkles added each year, with added venues and a later Super Bowl…on Valentine's Day.

But before we can get there, 272 regular-season games need to be played, with the full slate of 16 games starting this week. Heading into wk.1, here are the twelve QBs to play:

MORE: Bold NFL predictions for Week 1 of 2026 season

New York Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart (6) walks off the field at halftime during a preseason opening game between the New York Giants and Minnesota Vikings on Saturday, Aug. 15, 2026, at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, NJ.

The Giants begin the 2026 campaign at home against the Cowboys. I love taking home QBs, especially in wk.1 of the season. Taking a running QB is always a good call at the start of the season, because while accuracy may be down, speed is always there. And Dart can cause havoc with his legs. Dallas will look to come out of the gate strong, so Dart will be compelled to keep up.

The Texans start at home against the Bills. And while I think the Bills have a solid chance to leave Houston with a W, the Texans defense is one of the best in the league, and stand to get Stroud the ball with more than a few three and outs, and a couple of turnovers. Josh Allen will still get his points, forcing Stroud to throw often.

Allen faces off in a really tough matchup this week. He is on the road, heading to Houston. The Texans have one of the most tenacious and violent defenses in the league. And being wk.1 they are healthy. The consensus No. 1 QB in the league will rarely be this low, but it is because he is so great that he's even on this list this week.

Jan 4, 2026; Jacksonville, Florida, USA; Jacksonville Jaguars quarterback Trevor Lawrence (16) throws a pass against the Tennessee Titans during the third quarter at EverBank Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Travis Register-Imagn Images

The last time Lawrence left his home turf, he walked off with a loss in the playoffs. He won't have that problem in this game against the Browns.

The Browns ended last year as one of the worst teams in the league, and not much has changed this year. The Jags are 8.5 favorites in this game, and look for Lawrence to put up big numbers: 250+ passing yards and at least 2 TDs.

Stafford was the toughest QB to rank this week, due to the game against the 49ers being played in Australia. A game has never been played so far away, and after such a long flight, it remains to be seen how much it will affect the players.

Historically, though, whenever these two divisional rivals play, there are usually fireworks. The defending MVP will want to make the long trip worthwhile and start the year 1-0…as well as giving the Australian fans a show.

Mahomes will do whatever he can to not start the season 0-1 against a divisional opponent. On top of that, it's a Monday Night Game, which is where Mahomes shines. He always does his best work in primetime matchups.

Jan 18, 2026; Chicago, IL, USA; Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams (18) calls the snap count from shotgun formation against the Los Angeles Rams during the third quarter of an NFC Divisional Round game at Soldier Field. Mandatory Credit: Matt Marton-Imagn Images

Consensus is that Williams is going to have a breakout season coming off a very productive sophomore year with the Bears. His offensively minded HC Ben Johnson is talking about breaking the all-time scoring record, so he'll undoubtedly have a bag of tricks to accomplish it.

For a road game, Williams has a soft-landing spot, going top Carolina.  The Bears are a 3pt road dog, and the o/u is set at 47.5pts. The expectation is that p[points will be scored. Look for Williams to put up at least 27pts in this game.

The Seahawks put their Super Bowl banner into the rafters, in front of their ravenous fans. The "12" will be ready for blood, facing off against the Patriots in a Super Bowl rematch. With Kenneth Walker gone and relying on a rookie RB, more will be asked of Darnold.

With Christian Gonzalez just signing a new contract yesterday, he will be on the field for the Patriots, but Jaxon Smith-Njigba will look for payback after an underwhelming Super Bowl performance. Gonzalez has missed time this offseason and stands to be rusty. Darnold will get Smith-Njigba the ball early and often. Look for a similar result as the final score in the Super Bowl.

This game is going to put up pts like a pinball machine. New Orleans is a high-scoring team in their own right, and Las Vegas has the o/u set at 49.5 pts. HC Dan Campbell will want to come out of the gate on fire. They have a fairly easy opening day opponent at home. They are a 6.5 pt favorite. Look for them to easily cover, with Goff eclipsing 300 yds with a three-TD performance.

Los Angeles Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert (10) throws the ball against the Tennessee Titans during the third quarter at Nissan Stadium in Nashville, Tenn., Sunday, Nov. 2, 2025.

The Chargers have maybe the easiest game on the slate this week, facing off at home against the Cardinals. They are a huge 9.5 pt favorite. While HC Jim Harbaugh preaches a balanced attack, implementing a strong running game, this is the season he lets Herbert off the leash.

Herbert has the weapons all over the field with a stacked WR room, led by Ladd McConkey and Quentin Johnston. He has Omarian Hampton, who is a fantastic receiving RB out of the backfield. And he has a great allotment of TEs between David Njoku, Oronde Gadsen, and Charlie Kolar. Look for Harbert to put up over 30 pts with well over 300 passing yds and at least a couple of TDs.

In a divisional opening week matchup against the Commanders, a cloud seems to have been lifted in Philadelphia. The removal of AJ Brown is addition by subtraction for the Eagles. Hurts won't feel compelled to feed him the ball and can just play again. The team still has a plethora of receivers, and Saquon Barkley. And as I said about Jaxson Dart, especially in wk. 1,  a running QB has a great advantage.

Hurts will keep drives alive with his legs and wants to put on a show for the home team after a disappointing 2025 campaign. Hurts is projected to rush for 30.5 yds. Look for him to surpass that mark and get at least 50 yds on the ground. He'll score at least one rushing TD and add a couple passing TDs.

This game is going to be a shootout against the Buccaneers. Baker Mayfield recently signed an extension, which will be a huge lift off his shoulders, and he'll get his points, meaning Burrow will need to keep up. This is one of the highest pt totals of the week, with Vegas setting the o/u at 50.5 pts. I wouldn't be surprised to see this game into the 60s, with Burrow putting up 35pts with 3-4 TD passes.

The main concern for the Bengals has been the health of Ja'Marr Chase. He's been nursing his left knee since the end of August, but has practiced with the team over the last few days. He'll be ready for Opening Day, and so will Burrow.

title: Rams holding Aaron Donald out for Week 1 is the right decision
description: Rams DT Aaron Donald staying back in L.A. instead of flying to Australia is the right decision for the long haul
fullText:
The Los Angeles Rams announced on Tuesday that star defensive tackle Aaron Donald would not make the trip down to Melbourne, Australia, for the season opener, instead opting to continue his workout process as he gets ready for Week 2.

Donald returned to the Rams on Aug. 30, ending his retirement after two seasons. The decision to keep him back in L.A. was a tough one, but here's why it's a good thing that the three-time Defensive Player of the Year isn't playing.

Outside of the fact that Donald returned to practice less than two weeks ago following two years away from the game, the Rams' timeline and schedule will give them an advantage in his preparations.

Playing against the San Francisco 49ers would've been foolish in the long run, as the tight turnaround – paired with the travel to and from Australia – could have had negative effects on Donald's ability to play a whole season. On top of that, the 49ers' offensive scheme is predicated on their running game, something Donald may not have been as effective against compared to his teammates who have had a full camp and preseason to prepare for.

The 49ers also get the ball out quickly in the passing game, likely negating Donald's impact off the bench, especially as he has to knock off natural rust. Donald would've been schemed out anyways, and now the team's faster pass rushers will be able to see more of the field.

However, the biggest advantage comes after the game. The Rams play the 49ers on Thursday. They do not play again until Monday, September 21st. That will give Donald another week and a half of uninterrupted time to prepare. Instead of giving a returning legend a tough hurdle to climb in the early season, Donald will have had over three weeks to get right, especially as the Rams have a gauntlet to begin the season.

After the 49ers, the Rams play three playoff teams in their next four games, with trips to Denver and Philadelphia in back-to-back weeks.

So while it's unfortunate that Donald won't be on the field, there's a reason why the Rams are one of the healthier teams in football. Donald's inactive status for game day will pay off in the long run.

title: Arsenal Starting XI vs Napoli: Confirmed Team News and Predicted Lineup
description: Arsenal vs Napoli Predicted XI: Arteta Weighs Rotation for Champions League OpenerMikel Arteta has a decision to make in Naples. Arsenal start another Champions League campaign on Wednesday night, and...
fullText:
Mikel Arteta has a decision to make in Naples. Arsenal start another Champions League campaign on Wednesday night, and the issue is simple enough, rotate now or trust the same core again.

Last season offered encouragement and regret in equal measure. Arsenal won all eight league phase matches and went through the competition without losing in 90 minutes. They still finished short, beaten on penalties by Paris Saint-Germain in the final in Budapest. That is the standard now. Getting close carries no value on its own.

Arteta has the squad to change things without weakening the side too much. Bruno Guimaraes missed the Chelsea game after carrying a knock, and Martin Zubimendi looks the obvious candidate to come into midfield. Declan Rice should keep his place, with Martin Odegaard continuing as the organiser further forward.

On the left, Eberechi Eze is pushing for a start. Through the middle, Viktor Gyokeres could be handed his first start of the season if Arsenal choose to manage Kai Havertz carefully. That would be sensible rather than dramatic. Arsenal need freshness across this opening stretch.

The back line is where the options narrow. William Saliba is out with a back injury, Jurrien Timber has yet to play this season, and Cristhian Mosquera remains a doubt with a muscle problem. As a result, Ezri Konsa is expected to continue alongside Gabriel after starting in the win over Chelsea.

There could also be caution over Riccardo Calafiori. He has started the season well, but his injury record means Arsenal are unlikely to take unnecessary risks. Piero Hincapie was the only defender on the bench against Chelsea, and he looks a credible option to start at left-back.

Arteta is due to speak before the match and may offer more clarity, but the likely Arsenal team is clear enough: Raya; White, Konsa, Gabriel, Hincapie; Rice, Zubimendi; Saka, Odegaard, Eze; Gyokeres.

Kick-off is 8pm BST on Wednesday, September 9, 2026, at the Stadio Diego Armando Maradona. Arsenal's Champions League campaign starts with a proper test. Nothing extravagant, nothing soft, just a strong away game against serious opposition.

title: José Mourinho weighs in on Trent Alexander-Arnold's midfield stint in Champions League win
description: José Mourinho insists Trent Alexander-Arnold is 'not a midfielder' despite deploying him in the middle of the park during Real Madrid's UEFA Champions League win over Inter Milan
fullText:
José Mourinho maintains that Trent Alexander-Arnold is "not a midfielder" despite utilizing the ex-Liverpool player in that central role on Tuesday.

'The Special One' extended his encouraging beginning to his second tenure at the Santiago Bernabéu as Real Madrid defeated another of his former sides, Inter Milan, to claim all three points in their UEFA Champions League opener.

Mourinho was lacking midfield choices due to suspensions for Eduardo Camavinga, Arda Güler, and Bernardo Silva, which led him to think outside the box and deploy Alexander-Arnold alongside Federico Valverde in the engine room. The former Liverpool star featured in that position during his youth and has also filled that role with England on previous occasions.

Donovan and Howard weigh in on Balogun's failed Everton transfer after USMNT star calls off deal

Jamal Musiala breaks silence on 'seizures' after collapsing during consecutive Bayern Munich games

Gareth Southgate utilized him there during Euro 2024 before abandoning the trial after just two group stage matches while, throughout his Liverpool tenure, he frequently advanced into midfield, albeit from his right-back slot, and Mourinho evidently views him as a full-back, as per The Mirror.

The Portuguese manager commented: "He has played midfield with England and Liverpool... but he is not a midfielder. He has played very well. He has interpreted what he needed to really well, tactically. Both him and Valverde have worked very well at this level."

Alexander-Arnold created two chances and attempted more crosses than any other Real player during his time in midfield, yet failed to win a single tackle. His passing accuracy also dipped to 83.3 percent, something Mourinho attributed to the positional adjustment.

"He has lost some balls because it is not the same to play in this position compared to at right-back," he said. "The intensity of physical work is quite difficult. He has a different engine. He has given 100 percent. He left the pitch with nothing left to give."

Now on his third manager, Alexander-Arnold has faced fierce competition for a starting berth after enjoying an established role at Liverpool. title: Fantasy Football Week 1 Rankings: Hayden Winks' top-12 running back projections
description: Fantasy football analyst Hayden Winks reveals his top-12 running back rankings and analysis for Week 1.
fullText:
Fantasy football analyst Hayden Winks reveals his top-12 running back rankings and analysis for Week 1. He'll continue to update his rankings for every position throughout the week. He also wrote about his RB2 rankings for Week 1.

Gibbs has averaged 25.1 half PPR points in eight games that David Montgomery has missed, or played under 25% snaps. Not only is Monty gone, but Isiah Pacheco is now on injured reserve. This will be the most valuable role in fantasy football pretty clearly.

Gibbs is projected for 19.9 half PPR point on 118.5 total yards in the betting markets right now, and the Lions have the highest team total this week at 28.75 points.

The Saints are a feisty defense but not one to overly adjust to. Last year, they were worse against the run than to receiving RBs, which has been a trend in Brandon Staley defenses for years.

Join a Yahoo Fantasy Football league for the 2026 NFL season

Last year's RB2 on RB2 usage is set up for a similar season with Brian Robinson Jr. attempting to fill the Tyler Allgeier complementary, bruising role. It's possible Bijan doesn't have the full goal-line role, but we're here for the receptions (4.6 per game last year) and explosives.

The Falcons are only 28th in projected points this week in Pittsburgh, where they'll face off with one of the best defensive lines and a reworked secondary. Last year, the Steelers were the fourth-best fantasy RB defense when adjusting for schedule. It's one of the worst spots of the year, and Robinson will have Tua Tagovailoa in a new scheme to lead the offense.

Robinson is projected for 18.1 half PPR points and 113.5 total yards by the betting markets.

Last year's RB1 on RB1 usage opens the year in the other hemisphere against arguably the best DL in the NFL with Myles Garrett added; Aaron Donald won't play in the opener. McCaffrey averaged 2.5 and 2.6 yards per carry, respectively, in his matchups with the Rams last year, but he caught eight passes in each outing to save his fantasy outing.

A similar formula may be needed here with the 49ers listed as 3.5-point underdogs on the No. 18 team total. It looks like fourth-round LG Carver Willis will be starting next to the other four returning starters on the OL. McCaffrey is projected for 16.4 half PPR points by the betting markets.

Barkley has torched the Commanders as an Eagle. He's put up 132-1, 150-2 and 146-2 rushing lines on 21+ carries.

Washington is attempting to improve its run defense with first-round LB Sonny Styles, LB Leo Chenal, EDGE Odafe Oweh and DT Tim Settle added this offseason, but last year, opposing RB rooms averaged 20 more rushing yards per game than their season average, which was the third worst. In terms of schedule adjusted fantasy points allowed to RBs, Washington was fourth worst.

Equally as important, the Eagles' own offense looks better this year. The OL is healthy right now after missing a ton of time last season, and new OC Sean Mannion is likely tiers better than last year's static play-caller. Barkley should be closer to his 2024 RB1 overall finish than last year's RB14 overall finish this year.

Week 1 is a great time to get the party started. The Eagles are ninth in projected points as 4.5-points home favorites.

Achane will have one of the greatest workloads in fantasy football. The betting markets project Achane for a position-high 6.5 targets, and he's third in projected total yards (106.5) only behind the consensus 1.01 and 1.02 picks. Miami's top receivers are two Round 3 rookies and slot-only Malik Washington, so expect a ton of first-read targets to Achane, even if Malik Willis is more likely to scramble than Tagovailoa was.

Of course, the Dolphins only project for 18.5 points (31st), so Achane has to win with receiving and overall volume to maintain his RB5 per-game finish in PPR last year. Miami was only 25th in scoring last year when he did that, for what it's worth.

The matchup is fantastic. The Raiders were 25th against fantasy RBs last year because they struggled stopping the run. They changed out their starting LBs to fix that, but it's still a horrible starting DT combo. Give me LT Patrick Paul, first-round LG Kadyn Proctor and C Aaron Brewer over them, easily.

I like Achane for more than his projected 15.1 half PPR points.

I'm not sure the skill group (Daniel Jones, Alec Pierce, Josh Downs and Keenan Allen) can walk in a straight line without wobbling for different reasons, but it looks like the projected starting lineup will be available for Week 1.

The Colts will need them against a potentially great Ravens defense under new HC Jesse Minter, who was an elite defensive coordinator. Indianapolis is only projected for the 19th-most points at home after being first in scoring through Week 13 with Daniel Jones healthy last year.

Taylor was the RB1 on RB2 usage during that stretch, averaging 23.3 half-PPR points and 107 rushing yards. Insane. He's only projected for 15.3 half PPR points and 94.5 total yards this week because of the matchup and health uncertainty.

In 32 games with Lamar Jackson, Henry is the RB6 (17.4 half PPR points) on RB15 usage. He's the RB1 overall in rush yards over expected per carry (+37%) in those games because LJ is a threat to run and occupies one of the front-seven defenders. That's all it takes for Henry to get to top speed, and it's hard to stop a freight train.

The Colts are improved up front with second-round LB C.J. Allen and star DT DeForest Buckner healthy after just 10 games last year, and Indianapolis was league average in the advanced rushing metrics last year. It's not a bad matchup, it's just neutral.

The Ravens are sixth in projected points (25.5) in this road, domed environment as 3.5-point favorites. Henry has averaged 43 more rushing yards in career wins, 104 to 61. The Big Dog is projected for 14.4 half PPR points and 80.5 rushing yards by the betting markets.

Waiting on Keaton Mitchell news, but the Chargers are tied for first in projected points (28.75) this week at home against the Cardinals as 10-point favorites. The game script couldn't get better than this.

Arizona was seventh-worst against fantasy RBs last year, and they're mostly relying on improvements and better health up front to change things around.

Brown is the RB12 on RB5 usage over the past two seasons in 21 games with Joe Burrow active, using half-PPR scoring. It's even better in just 2025, when Brown was the RB5 on RB4 usage in his six games with Burrow. Recent investments in the Bengals OL has paved the way to better short-yardage success, and their offseason pivot to more under-center runs is a commitment to finding more explosives on the ground. It's a great situation for Brown.

The opening matchup is tougher with first-round EDGE Rueben Bain, DT A'Shawn Robinson and two veteran starting LBs added to a front that features star DT Vita Vea. Last year's unit was worse, and opposing RB rooms averaged 16 fewer yards than their season average against Tampa Bay. Rushing yards will be difficult to find this week. At the same time, the Bucs allowed a league-high 19 more receiving yards per game to RB rooms compared to their league average. That plays into Brown's strengths. As a whole, the Bucs were 19th against fantasy RBs.

The Bengals, while healthy, are a total unit. They're projected for the third most points (27.0) this week as 3.5-point home favorites. Brown projects for 14.7 half PPR points in the betting markets, the eighth most.

With Patrick Mahomes (ACL) returning from major surgery and with only fifth-round rookie Emmett Johnson behind him, Walker is set for an elite workload. As the Seahawks bell cow during their Super Bowl run, Walker averaged 23.0 PPR points (RB3) on 18.9 expected points (RB5). Those are similar numbers to what the peak RBs under coach Andy Reid put up before the Chiefs ignored and whiffed on the position in recent years. Remember Jamaal Charles, LeSean McCoy, Brian Westbrook, Kareem Hunt, Deuce Staley? I do. Well, not Staley (personally too young).

The opening matchup is difficult, however. The Broncos were sixth-best against fantasy RBs when adjusting for schedule. They are without EDGE Jonathan Cooper right now and lost DT2 John Franklin-Meyers this offseason, at least. Because Denver is so elite at man coverage and use it at the highest rate (45% last year), the Chiefs are encouraged to run the ball in neutral situations, as their top receivers are horrible against press man.

Walker is projected for 82.5 total yards, while the Chiefs are 13th in projected points (23.25) at home on Monday Night Football. I like the higher on 2.5 receptions. Reid used to love the RB screen. Those get brought back this year.

Waiting on Kyle Monangai's official status after he had a hyper-extended knee on Aug. 17, but even if he's able to grit it out, Monangai is probably looking at a smaller role in the opener than he had last year. Even while splitting time, Swift was the RB13 on RB17 usage from Week 5 on, when the Bears started figuring things out in HC Ben Johnson's first season. Swift was the RB5 in success rate during that stretch, showing better vision while running behind a great OL. Their most-important three linemen return.

The matchup is great, too. The Bears are seventh in projected points (24.75), and the Panthers were rough against the run last year. They did add EDGE1 Jaelan Phillips and LB1 Devin Lloyd this offseason, so they'll likely be more average than bad this year.

Swift is top-10 in projected fantasy points (14.1 half PPR) per the betting markets on a projected 86.5 total yards.

As the clear starter last year, Williams was the RB13 on RB6 usage using half PPR scoring. Nothing has changed? Same HC, OC, QB, OL (minus LG Tyler Smith), WRs and TEs. The Cowboys were fifth in scoring in 2025, and they're fifth in projected points this week at home against the Giants.

It's an eruption spot. New York should be improved against the run under HC John Harbaugh with some new pieces, but they also lost star DT Dexter Lawrence. The Giants were the worst schedule-adjusted defense against fantasy RBs. Dead last. They were also last in EPA per carry allowed.

title: Mariners Rookie Hits Longest Home Run In T-Mobile Park History; Tied For Longest Home Run This Season
description: The Seattle Mariners lost 10-5 on Tuesday night, but a rookie hit a 474-foot home run
fullText:
The Seattle Mariners lost 10-5 on Tuesday to the Texas Rangers, but rookie Lazaro Montes hit a 474-foot home run that is making headlines.

The no-doubter is the longest home run at T-Mobile Park since Statcast tracking started in 2015, per MLB.com's Luke Olson. Montes tied Fernando Tatis Jr.'s home run against the Atlanta Braves on July 21 for the longest home run hit in the majors this season.

474 FOOT BOMB FROM LAZ.

Montes' first home run at @tmobilepark is the longest in ballpark Statcast history and tied for the longest in MLB this season. 🤯 pic.twitter.com/kzCrVyoZDv

"Right when I hit it, I said, 'Oh man, this is far,'" Montes said after the game.

Montes was called up when the rosters expanded on Sept. 1. The 21-year-old outfielder checks in at 6-foot-5, 250 pounds, and is the team's No. 5 prospect. He had 38 home runs between Double-A Arkansas and Triple-A Tacoma in the minor leagues this season, and has two home runs in the big leagues now. He has a 65-grade power tool, and it is showing early on in the big leagues.

Looking for the perfect gift for a baseball player in your life? Check out our brand-new baseball lifestyle brand!

In six games so far, he has a .819 OPS, but his batting average is just .219. He has six RBIs and a walk as well, but he knows he can be playing better.

"Not bad. Not bad," Montes said, reacting to his stats. "Can be better."

T-Mobile Park is known for suppressing power, so Montes' home run is no small feat. The Mariners are 6 1/2 games out of a wild card spot with 17 games left to play. The hope was that a power bat like Montes' could help them get into the postseason, but it's looking unlikely.
