title: Israel tells Britain to close East Jerusalem consulate within 30 days, officials say
description: Israel has told Britain it must close its East Jerusalem consulate within a month, Israeli officials said on Wednesday, as a retaliatory step against
fullText:
TEL AVIV, Sept 9 (Reuters) - Israel has told Britain it must close its East Jerusalem consulate within a month, Israeli officials said on Wednesday, as a retaliatory step against sanctions that Britain, France and Canada have announced against settlements.

The sanctions are among the strongest collective actions taken by major Western ‌allies of Israel over Israeli settlements, and have prompted intense pushback in Israel weeks before it holds a general election.

While the effect of the sanctions may be ‌mostly symbolic, they highlight Israel's growing isolation among countries it once counted as close allies over its war in Gaza and expansion of settlements in the West Bank.

The U.S. ambassador to Israel, Mike Huckabee, a staunch supporter of Israel, ​has condemned the sanctions and accused the British government of "Jew hate", but neither the White House nor the State Department issued strong criticism of the move.

Two Israeli officials and two other sources familiar with the matter said London had been given 30 days to close the consulate, which represents Britain in Jerusalem, the West Bank and Gaza on Palestinian issues.

Israel has also barred 12 British politicians from visiting the country, told British officials and diplomats in the West Bank and a Gaza coordination centre in Israel to leave, and said Britain can no longer train Palestinian security forces in ‌the West Bank.

It has not yet announced actions against France or ⁠Canada, which joined Britain in saying they will halt trade with settlements, or against nine other countries that endorsed the UK sanctions.

Although the UK sanctions were widely anticipated, Israeli parliamentary opposition leader Yair Lapid said on Tuesday that "no one knew" the other countries were going to endorse the move.

British ⁠Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband said on Wednesday he regretted Israel's decision to order the consulate to close, but that it was not a surprise.

"We weighed the costs and benefits of acting (...) and we thought we simply could not stand by because we feared Israeli action," he told BBC TV.

On Tuesday Miliband, describing himself as a "proud British Jew", said that Israel had "turned a blind eye" to violence carried out by ​settlers ​against Palestinians and that Britain's move was aimed at keeping alive a two-state solution to the Israeli-Palestinian conflict.

Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's office did not respond to a ‌request for comment on the consulate closure.

Israel's Foreign Minister Gideon Saar said on X that he had thanked Kemi Badenoch, the leader of the British opposition Conservative Party, for her criticism of the sanctions.

Badenoch wrote in the Sun newspaper that the Labour government was "putting its own party-political ­interests ahead of our national interest".

Saar had earlier called the action by Britain "morally distorted" and accused the UK of "blatant interference in the affairs of a sovereign state and its electoral process".

Miliband on Tuesday told lawmakers that, in addition to banning imports of goods from Israeli settlements in the West Bank, the UK would also take measures against companies and individuals providing services to settlements including "construction, infrastructure, financing, or real estate".

France and Canada said they too would ban the import of products ‌from Israeli settlements, while nine other countries including Denmark and Portugal endorsed the British action.

There has so ​far been a muted response from the United States, with U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio saying Washington did ​not want to see "anything destabilising" in the West Bank while declining to specifically comment ​on the UK sanctions.

Britain's chief rabbi condemned the UK sanctions as a "truly dark day". Yachad, a British Jewish group formed to support ‌a two-state solution, said that the announcement was "not anti-Israel, and it is ​certainly not antisemitic," accusing Israel's "extremist government" of crossing almost ​every "red line" to entrench its "occupation".

The sanctions are widely regarded by diplomats as an important but symbolic step, with goods from Israeli settlements making up only a fraction of Israel's exports, but the move highlights Israel's growing diplomatic isolation.

Israel's government has faced mounting international condemnation over Israel's conduct in the war in Gaza, in which tens of thousands ​of Palestinians have been killed since October 2023, and more recently ‌over Israel's expansion of settlements and rising settler violence against Palestinians in the West Bank.

Britain, France and Canada were among countries that in 2025 formally recognised ​the State of Palestine and have previously imposed sanctions targeting settlements and Israeli ministers over accusations of inciting violence against Palestinians.

title: Tesla crashes into scaffolding in Midtown Manhattan, killing passenger
description: Two 27-year-old females were in the vehicle when it crashed.
fullText:
A Tesla crashed into scaffolding in Midtown Manhattan on Wednesday morning, killing the vehicle's passenger and sending the driver to the hospital, according to police.

A preliminary police investigation revealed that a gray 2024 Tesla Model Y SUV driven by a 27-year-old female collided with scaffolding, a bus stop and a mailbox at approximately 2:43 a.m. on Wednesday, a New York Police Department spokesperson told ABC News.

The driver was traveling eastbound on East 42nd Street and failed to navigate the roadway, police said.

Emergency medical services responded on the scene and transported the driver and a 27-year-old female passenger to the hospital, where the passenger was pronounced dead and the driver is in stable condition, according to police.

Feds launch probe into Tesla's deployment of Cybercab vehicles with no brakes and steering wheels

What caused the driver to lose control of the vehicle is unknown at this time, according to police. The driver was taken into custody and the investigation is ongoing.

The heavily damaged Tesla was shown by traffic cameras in the street where the vehicle came to a stop after traveling several blocks following the initial collision, police said.

The NYPD's Highway District Collision Investigation Squad is handling the investigation.

title: A NYC firehouse was first to respond on 9/11. 25 years on, Sal Argano is the last still on staff
description: Sal Argano got lucky.  When the World Trade Center was struck by hijacked jets on Sept. 11, 2001, the New York City firefighter was in Brooklyn, on loan to another station, rather than at his usual po...
fullText:
NEW YORK (AP) — Sal Argano got lucky. When the World Trade Center was struck by hijacked jets on Sept. 11, 2001, the New York City firefighter was in Brooklyn, on loan to another station, rather than at his usual post at the small Manhattan firehouse just across an intersection from the twin towers.

He rushed downtown to find his firehouse badly damaged but still standing. Six of its members, he'd later learn, were among the 343 New York City firefighters killed in the World Trade Center's collapse.

"If I wasn't sent out on rotation there would have been a good chance I would not be here today," Argano says. "I think about that all the time."

Almost 25 years later, Argano, now 65, is still on duty at the firehouse — the last of the firefighters assigned there in 2001 who still works there.

Today, the crews at the firehouse respond to emergency calls but also serve as a de facto part of the 9/11 memorial, visited by crowds of tourists daily.

Some visitors come specifically to see the large bronze relief along the side of the building listing the names of the firefighters killed on 9/11.

Others pause to take selfies as they pass by on their way to the National 9/11 Memorial plaza across the street, drawn by the sight of Engine 10 and Ladder 10, the gleaming trucks sitting in the garage that give the station its nickname: Ten House.

"This is definitely one of those companies where if you don't want to ingratiate yourself to the public, it's definitely not the right place," said Capt. Terence Brody, who commands Ladder 10 and has worked at the station since 2016. "People around the world know this firehouse. They're going to come by and say hello."

Brody, now 55, was still in the fire academy on 9/11. Cadets grabbed their gear and were bused to ground zero.

The debris hung so thickly in the air around the fallen towers that it looked like it was snowing, he said.

"It was a beautiful sunny Tuesday, and then you're in this kind of apocalyptic atmosphere," Brody said. "It was a little overwhelming, to say the least."

In the days after the attack, Ten House served as both command center and safe space for weary first responders, he said. As the years passed, its crew had a front-row seat to the area's rebirth.

Robert Favata joined Ladder 10 in 2008, fresh out of the academy.

In those early years, he worked beside a giant hole teeming with construction activity. Now 46, he looks out at a transformed landscape.

A pair of waterfall pools sit in the footprint of the old towers, ringed by parapets etched with the names of nearly 3,000 victims. Below ground, the 9/11 Museum houses mangled steel beams, a destroyed fire truck and other artifacts. New skyscrapers ring the memorial.

"When I got here, there was nothing," Favata says. "I never thought they were gonna finish."

Argano can be found most days perched near the station's open bay doors, patiently answering questions, shaking hands and posing for photos.

He says Ten House firefighters have a unique charge: they're both living testimonials to the events of 9/11 as well as public faces of the centuries-old FDNY.

Argano says he tries to impress on younger firefighters — many increasingly not even born before the attacks — the importance of treating every visitor with respect.

"This is not like any other firehouse," he said. "We have our fire duty, we have our responses, and then we have a responsibility toward the people outside."

He acknowledges the task is not always easy. The packs of gawking tourists can be relentless. Their questions can sometimes come across too personal, too insincere or just simply too out there.

Many of the younger firefighters tend to keep a lower profile for that reason, he said.

After responding to an early morning call this particular day, most of the crew heads to the back of the station to stow their gear or upstairs to help prepare lunch.

Argano meanwhile chats up a firefighter from France and his wife and then invites them into the station.

He points to a wall of patches from fire departments across the world that have been gifted over the years, as well as the well-worn helmets hanging in the rafters.

At another point, though, a lady asks — perhaps a bit too flippantly — what's so special about Ten House.

Argano shrugs: "It's just a fire station." After she departs, he says it simply wasn't worth the effort.

"If I need to explain to you all of that, then it's like, 'Pull up a seat'," Argano said. "Let me get another cigarette. It's gonna be a long one."

Favata considers the approaching 25th anniversary as likely one of his last before retirement. He worries, though, if he's done enough to keep the memories of Ten House alive.

"When I got here, so many of the guys worked 9/11 and they told me their stories of that day," Favata said, choking on tears. "I just hope I can give like a percentage of what they've told me to the younger guys."

Brody, meanwhile, handed in his retirement papers Tuesday. His last day will be in October.

"It's interesting to think that my first day in the field was right across the street, and this is where I'm gonna end my career," said Brody, who writes screenplays in his spare time and has already had two of them turned into Hallmark Channel movies.

But Argano, who drives Engine 10, isn't quite ready to pack it in. He fears something will be lost when no one is there who still remembers.

"I'm not done. I'm gonna be here as long as I can," Argano said. "I'm going to keep telling them what I know, what I saw, what I've been through. Telling them the history of this firehouse. Everything I can remember."

Follow Philip Marcelo at https://x.com/philmarcelo

title: Socialist politicians are 'more racist than the KKK,' says Black Dem official urging voters to ditch El-Sayed
description: Karen Whitsett slams Abdul El-Sayed and Democratic Party leaders she says take Black voters for granted, calling out his ties to Hasan Piker.
fullText:
An elected Democratic official in Michigan is rallying her community against U.S. Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed and claims those within the socialist rise of her party take Black voters for granted.

"It doesn't change, it's just different slave owners," Democratic Michigan state Rep. Karen Whitsett told Fox News Digital in reference to Democratic Party leaders who believe Black voters are a monolith who should only support left-wing candidates.

She claimed that El-Sayed is not working in the best interest of Black Michiganders and that the far-left wing of her party is "more racist than the KKK."

Jasmine Crockett Warns Democrats Are Too Focused On White Voters, Ignoring Black Voters

Whitsett called out prominent Black voices known for rallying the community's vote for Democrats — specifically naming Al Sharpton and controversial Detroit pastor Horace Sheffield III, an El-Sayed campaign surrogate. She accused the pair of working to "keep the knee on [Black voters'] neck."

Whitsett said Black voters are "waking up" and are "realizing the power of our vote."

"You can see the serious divide of the crazy socialist far-left and especially the White women," Whitsett said. "They are the worst and the most racist that there possibly ever could be. They're, I think, they're more racist than the KKK."

"Are you trying to help the Black community or are you trying to kill it?" she rhetorically asked. "Are you trying to keep people stupid and ill-informed or what? Because right now I can't tell, right? Is this voter education or are you just trying to make sure you count your slaves on the plantation."

Michigan Gop Lawmaker Casts Doubt On El-sayed's Socialist Denial As Policies Tell Another Story: 'Sharp Odds'

El-Sayed's values aren't aligned with hers, Whitsett said, adding that she doesn't think he has the best interest of Black voters at heart, either.

"I'm going to stand on Bible first, and I'm going to stand on community first," she said. I don't care about moving up within the Democratic Party. I don't care about making sure my pockets are better."

El-Sayed's campaign did not return Fox News Digital's request for comment on Whitsett's criticism of the candidate and the Democratic Party's leftward shift.

Whitsett is not running for re-election and will retire when her term expires at the end of the year.

"I always try to be a voice of reason, and I'm not a go along, get along. So, my whole thing is it has to make sense, and I am definitely family over party. God over party is of the utmost importance," she said.

"So for me, when you point that out to people, it's just common sense that to people, that's just common sense that El-Sayed is not the candidate," she continued. "There's just no way. It doesn't line up. It doesn't line up Biblically, and it doesn't line up with common sense."

Noting that she does believe everyone should have medical insurance, Whitsett harped on El-Sayed's campaign promise of Medicare for All. She said the progressive candidate hasn't adequately explained how that system will be implemented, and what it means for Americans when they visit the doctor.

El-sayed Tries To Make Peace With Jewish Democrats But Draws Line At Dumping Hasan Piker

"This Medicare for All, it's not for all. It's not going to change the dynamics of how many doctors there are, or nurses or blood draws or anything else. You're now going to put the government in your health system, and they're going to decide for you."

El-Sayed already finds himself in hot water for palling around on the campaign trail with socialist Twitch streamer Hasan Piker, who said in 2019 that "America deserved 9/11." He has also praised Mao Zedong and Communist China, said capitalists should be murdered in the streets and is known for making antisemitic comments.

El-Sayed has refused to condemn Piker, instead painting him as a "streamer from California" who has no bearing on the race in Michigan, despite inviting Piker to Michigan to campaign for him.

Many Jewish Democrats in Michigan have vowed not to support the far-left candidate, saying in an open letter they feel "threatened and alienated by the politics and allies embraced by Abdul El-Sayed, which has included demonization of Jews, equivocation on terrorism, exclusion of Jewish Americans from public life, and expression of implacable hatred of the world's only Jewish nation."

title: Is the Iran-backed terrorist movement Hezbollah on the ropes in Lebanon?
description: Israel's capture of the Ali al-Taher ridge dealt a severe blow to Iran's Axis of Resistance, but experts warn Hezbollah is still rebuilding.
fullText:
JERUSALEM — With Israel's stunning capture of the strategically valuable Ali al-Taher ridge in south Lebanon on Sunday, a major Hezbollah and Iran stronghold, the campaign to degrade Tehran's so-called "Axis of Resistance" suffered a severe blow.

While the Israel Defense Forces (IDF) triumph is not a death blow, it means that the Iranian-regime-backed Hezbollah terrorist movement lost one of its key offensive bases to plan an invasion of Israel.

IDF Lt. Col. (Res.) Sarit Zehavi, the founder and president of the Israel-based Alma Research and Education Center (Alma), told Fox News Digital that "In the past three years Israel has attacked Hezbollah against various areas, for instance, we degraded the amount of rockets and missiles."

Exclusive: Israel Seizes Vast Iran Terror Axis Arsenal With Surprising Foreign Origins

She noted that the IDF has decimated 90% of Hezbollah's rocket and missile arsenal. Zehavi said, "Today Hezbollah is holding between 10,000 to 15,000 rockets, which is much less than what it used to have. Most of the array of sophisticated missiles, accurate missiles and long-range missiles was either eliminated or neutralized."

She said, "The capability to launch an invasion of thousands of terrorists into Israel which was the plan, and this was the preparedness three years ago. This capability doesn't exist anymore since the IDF is based in South Lebanon along the borderline, preventing Hezbollah from coming back to those places."

In late August, Alma released a widely read analysis on: "Hezbollah – Situation Assessment: From a Large-Scale Terrorist Army to a Persistent Dispersed Threat."

Zehavi, who resides in northern Israel and has experienced Hezbollah's massive aerial attacks into her region since the Lebanese terrorist movement joined Hamas in its war against Israel, warned that, "As long as Iran supports its main proxy, which is Hezbollah, it will be very difficult to prevent its rebuilding of its military capabilities and with everything that happened in Iran In the past year, Iran still supports Hezbollah."

She noted that Iran still aids Hezbollah via "arms smuggling and money" and "they still put a lot of effort [into] that and the training and the involvement of Iran in Hezbollah in Lebanon. And this must be stopped."

Lebanon Accuses Iran Of Inserting Irgc Terrorists Into Country 'Under Guise Of Diplomatic Activity'

Iran's regime is a state-sponsor of terrorism and Hezbollah's base is the Shiite community in Lebanon. Radical Shiite Islamism unifies Iran's regime with its chief proxy, Hezbollah, in Lebanon.

Alma, who has a deep knowledge of Hezbollah's activities, wrote on X on Sunday: "The battle for the Ali al-Taher Ridge is over – the struggle with Hezbollah is not."

According to Zehavi, Hezbollah "today is much more of a guerrilla organization than a terrorist army as it used to be. It is having a lot of difficulties in rebuilding its capabilities… It is dedicated to rebuilding its military capabilities. But it has a lot of challenges along the way with this regard because of the regime change in Syria, because of that fact that it's much more difficult to transfer weapons through the airport in Lebanon and through Syria. But it doesn't mean that it is not happening. They are still trying and some of it do pass."

Hezbollah's setback was also echoed by Israel TV's Channel 12 chief political analyst, Amit Segal. He said the Hezbollah base Ali al-Taher was "Just 10 kilometers (just over six miles) from the Israeli border, with a clear view of the Litani and the Israeli Hula Valley, it was the place from which Hezbollah intended to coordinate its own Oct. 7 in the Galilee."

Hezbollah's ally, the Hamas terrorist organization, invaded Israel nearly three years ago on Oct. 7 and slaughtered over 1,200 people in southern Israel, including more than 40 Americans.

The IDF announced on Sunday that "Soldiers from the 36th Division have operated in recent weeks to clear and neutralize the two underground routes in the Ali al-Taher Ridge area in the Security Zone. The soldiers achieved operational control of the ridge area, both above and below ground, and cleared the area of terrorists. Some of the terrorists were eliminated, while others fled the area."

Pentagon Hosts First-ever Israeli–lebanese Military Talks Aimed At Curbing Hezbollah

The IDF statement added that "Following operations in the underground routes over the past several weeks, their capability to carry out terror attacks against Israeli civilians and IDF soldiers from within the routes has been neutralized."

Hezbollah official Mahmoud Qamati told a Lebanese podcaster in late August that, "Ali al-Taher is important, but if it is lost it does not mean the end of Hezbollah."

Lebanon's Deputy Prime Minister Tarek Mitri told an Arab TV station, also in late August, that the Lebanese army was ready to take over the strategic ridge.

He accused Israel of blocking the army due to its own political considerations ahead of Israeli national elections on Oct. 27.

"The problem is not in the Lebanese army's readiness but in Israel's stance," he said.

The Trump administration had pushed for Hezbollah to allow Lebanon's Army to take control of Ali al-Taher. Hezbollah refused the proposed U.S. deal.

A State Department spokesperson told Fox News Digital that "Hizballah has been the primary obstacle to Lebanon's economic recovery, the main blemish on its international reputation, and the biggest threat to the safety and stability of Lebanon. It bears sole responsibility for Israel's presence on Lebanese soil. This is precisely why Hizballah must be disarmed and dismantled."

Experts Urge Extreme Caution On Iran's 'Crown Jewel' Hezbollah — Terror Group With Us Blood On Its Hands

The State Department spokesperson added that "Hizballah is drastically weaker than at any point in recent history, which has allowed the Government of Lebanon to outlaw its military activities. We fully support that decision, as do all of our regional partners."

Hanin Ghaddar, a senior fellow at The Washington Institute who focuses on Shia politics throughout the Levant, told Fox News Digital that "Hezbollah is weakened on two levels. They lost a lot of people, commanders and people, and weapons. Today, there is a goal to rebuild this military structure, invest in rebuilding in personnel, infrastructure and weapons. This is their primary goal."

Ghaddar, who is from Lebanon, added the second level of weakness for Hezbollah is the people are divided within the Shiite community. Hezbollah is no longer the father figure. Hezbollah ended with [Hassan] Nasrallah with his assassination. Hezbollah as protector and liberator is no longer there. It is a mix of IRGC [Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps], Hezbollah and Nabih Berri [ the Shiite speaker of the Lebanese parliament and the president of the Amal movement]."

Ghaddar said the Shiite community in Lebanon is fractured over whether to continue its support for Hezbollah after multiple wars with Israel.  She said it's "divided over whether Hezbollah is the solution. There is where Hezbollah is bleeding. Hezbollah needs the Shiite community for political power."

Ghaddar said that "Hezbollah has managed to get appointments through their allies, Berri and Amal… They have ministries of finance and health ministry… They really wanted appointments in general security and military. They got that. This reflects their strength economically. They are in survival and using power in the state and cash economy to rebuild."

Multiple Fox News Digital press queries sent to the Lebanese Embassy in Washington, D.C., went unanswered.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

title: Pearl-Cohn announcer Catfish is James Brown of high school football
description: Orlando 'Catfish' Pender Jr. has been announcing football games at Pearl-Cohn High since the 1990s.
fullText:
Editor's note: The Tennessean is running a season-long, all-access series about the Pearl-Cohn football program. To follow along with the project, please 

Catfish will not, does not, cannot sit down.

Are you kidding? Catfish is all movement.

Orlando "Catfish" Pender Jr. is 82, born during World War II, raised in a family of share croppers in "North Crackalackin," he says.

"That's North Carolina," he explains with a wink.

Dressed all in Firebird red except for the black sneakers that never stop. There is a chair, right there, in the announcer's booth at Pearl-Cohn High School. But that chair might as well be his grave. Catfish will sit when he's dead.

Instead, the Pearl-Cohn stadium announcer for more than three decades bops around the booth, smacking the wall on a bad play, leaping to celebrate a touchdown, lunging to slap high fives with the scoreboard operator.

You've never heard a stadium announcer like Catfish.

"Get that fire started," he growls at the defense. "The fire has started. Let it buuuurrrrrnnnnn."

He's singing, dancing, smiling ... disappointed, depressed, mumbling ... the entire game, depending on the success or failure of his beloved Pearl-Cohn Firebirds.

Catfish says he announces football games like James Brown, the energetic belter of songs back in the day. All sweat, grunts and gyrations.

Catfish holds the microphone to his chest and begins a slow rumble.

"Come on ... Come on ... Come on ... Pearl-Cohn kickoff team. STAY IN YOUR LANE." He delivers that last line in the high baritone range.

And oh goodness if somebody fumbles, especially if that fumble is recovered by the Firebirds, Catfish breaks into a scream that sounds like someone set off fireworks in a thunderstorm.

"Fumblerooski is my favorite," Catfish says in a calmer moment.

There are other Catfish signature vocal gems. For the last two seasons, the Firebirds quarterback has been L.J. Funk, who appears to have been put on this earth just so Catfish, upon the completing of a Funk touchdown pass, can break into song.

"We want the Funk, gotta have that Funk," he sings like George Clinton sang in the disco days as the Pearl-Cohn crowd goes wild. Catfish dances around the booth like he's just won at karaoke night.

There is a church choir in his background, as you might guess, and encounters with Chuck Berry, Janis Joplin, Jimi Hendrix and other music icons.

Catfish met The Tennessean on a rainy Wednesday afternoon, telling his life story while he paced the floor of his home in North Nashville, the one with the "million dollar view" of downtown. Standing on his front porch, he can see the AT&T (Batman) Building.

He said the place was overgrown with weeds so high no one could see the "For Sale" sign when he bought it.

He owns "Catfish Moving Company," with four trucks and 12 employees. He's been married twice and is currently single. He has five children, 15 grandchildren and eight great-grandchildren.

And he's got songs. He points to his back room, a man cave, of sorts, where he keeps his songs, awards and pictures that go way back.

"I've got 250 songs," he says, most are gospel tunes. "I've got four songs in my head right now. 'I'm a soldier in the Army of the Lord.'"

You wouldn't know it by watching this happy blur of a man. But he has had to lean on his religion in recent years. Since the one tragic moment that stopped Catfish from moving.

The moment from which he is just now recovering.

Catfish bends at the waist, arms dangling in front of him. He's standing in his living room, reenacting the story that got him his nickname.

He had 11 siblings, and when you grow up on a tobacco, corn, cotton and barley farm in Wilson, North Carolina, you are responsible to bring home something for dinner. At first, he tried a homemade fishing pole with a bent safety pin as a hook. But he didn't have a cork to make the hook float, so he scrapped that idea.

That's why he's bent over in his living room, mimicking his movements as a child. Arms dangling in a stream, he would wait motionless until he could grab a catfish with his bare hands.

"You didn't come home empty handed," he said.

Just about as long as he can remember, he's been Catfish.

He played high school football, but he was 

It was 1963 when a 19-year-old Catfish went to Philadelphia to see the big city. That's when he said he heard the words, "Go in the service now." He said it was the voice of God.

Think about the timing. Catfish joined the Marines just before the buildup in Vietnam. He said he became a chauffeur. His job took him to Naples, Nice, Palermo, Istanbul, Beruit. "I went to Greece," he said. "I'm walking in the paths of Plato and Socrates."

"If I would have gone to Vietnam, I would be dead," he said.

He said he ended his service in 1967 after a year in the Military Police in Quantico, Virginia.

In the 1960s and '70s, he found himself bouncing around America. In New York City's Greenwich Village, he formed "The King Biscuit Blues Band" and he covered Muddy Waters songs. He said he was on the circuit with Hendrix, Joplin and Otis Redding.

In San Francisco, he formed a new band "The New Wave."

"I was the Black Paul McCartney," he said.

He tried LSD once. He said his eyes became kaleidoscopes, and he sat still. "I couldn't move," he said.

It was the fear of what drugs might do to him, and the deaths of Jimi, Janis and Jim Morrison that convinced him to settle down.

Catfish chose Nashville as the place to raise his family. There was Jaqueline, Jalonda, Orlando III, Apryll and Briana.

Nashville, he knew, was a good place to play gospel music. He joined the Born Again Church on West Trinity Lane and sang in the choir.

That choir was a powerhouse. They made a live album featuring gospel star CeCe Winans with other stars like Israel Houghton, Desmond Pringle, Steve Crawford and Da'dra Greathouse.

And Orlando "Catfish" Pender Jr.

The album was nominated for a Grammy in 2004.

As he talks, he has pride in his eyes.

It just so happened that the Born Again Church meetings were in the Pearl-Cohn High School auditorium.

At first, Catfish volunteered to be a sideline videographer for the Firebirds football team.

Then he became the mascot. He was in his 50s, but there was Catfish jumping around the sideline in a bird hat with red wings.

"I fell in love with Pearl-Cohn," he said. "And yes, I had feathers."

He said coach Maurice Fitzgerald loved his voice, so he asked Catfish to be the public address announcer.

Catfish brought an energy to the booth that may be unfamiliar to fans who only hear monotone "First and 10" from most stadium announcers.

"I gotta do me," Catfish said. He loves when Pearl-Cohn whips an opponent, and still the opposing fans thank him for the energy he brings.

"The gift I have is my voice," he said. "I'm not saying something that's stale ... Elvis wanted to be the best. James Brown wanted to be the best. I want to be the best at something."

Pearl-Cohn football statistician Calvin Peters said Catfish brings the entertainment.

"He means the world to Pearl-Cohn," Peters said. "He brings a certain flair like no one else. His sayings and quotes are legendary."

Catfish stops when he talks about Janaye.

His granddaughter was in the Pearl-Cohn marching band, another in the long line of his relatives raised on Firebird football. She played the piccolo, following in the footsteps of her mother Jalonda, who played the clarinet.

Janaye was 31 in 2023 when she died due to a fentanyl overdose.

"I wasn't prepared for it," Orlando Pender Jr. says.

The happiest man you will ever meet didn't know how to deal with it.

"I went through denial, grief and torment," he said. "My heart was finally broken."

As football season begins again, he said Catfish has come back.

"He has sustained his spirit," said Pearl-Cohn head football coach Tony Brunetti. "He has a strong mind, a strong soul."

A smile appears on Catfish's face.

"I feel invincible," he says. "But I am not."

title: Jadarian Price makes his NFL debut today. A former teammate expects big things
description: Jadarian Price is making his NFL debut in the Seahawks' season opener against the Patriots. His former teammate is bullish about his NFL potential.
fullText:
Jadarian Price is looking to prove the Seattle Seahawks right for making him the first running back the team has selected in the first round of the NFL draft since Rashaad Penny in 2018.

At least one of Price's former teammates believes he will be able to find high-level success in the NFL.

Jeremiyah Love, who played with Price during their time together at Notre Dame, is bullish about his former counterpart's NFL prospects, as he told USA TODAY Sports in an April interview as part of his partnership with New Balance.

"I tell everybody this. I feel like JD can do everything I can do, if not more," Love said, referring to Price by his nickname.

Love expressed confidence in Price's skills as a runner, pass-catcher and blocker. He also referred to the 22-year-old as the best return man in the country, saying that Price returns kicks "way better than me."

That's why the No. 3 overall selection in the 2026 NFL Draft believes his first-round counterpart will be able to handle all that's required of an NFL running back, like himself.

"JD is a back that can do everything," Love said. "You give him a hole, he's gonna take that hole and he's gonna take it all the way to the house. JD's that type of back."

The Seahawks are certainly banking on that being the case. They drafted Price, in part, to help replace departed Super Bowl 60 MVP Kenneth Walker III, who signed with the Kansas City Chiefs in free agency.

Meanwhile, Walker's foil, Zach Charbonnet, is coming off a torn ACL and will miss at least the first four games of the season while on the physically unable to perform (PUP) list.

That should give Price an early chance to prove his former teammate turned division rival right and stake a claim to Seattle's top running back role for the foreseeable future.

Here's more to know about Price as he makes his NFL debut during the Seahawks' season opener against the New England Patriots.

Price played three college seasons at Notre Dame but largely played second fiddle to Love. During his final season, Price logged 113 carries for 674 yards and 11 touchdowns while adding 87 yards and two touchdowns on six catches. He also posted two kick return touchdowns on 12 return attempts with an FBS-best average of 37.5 yards per return.

Below is a full look at Price's stats across his three seasons with the Fighting Irish:

Price's strong performance helped convince the Seahawks to select him with the 32nd overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft. He was the final pick of the first round while he and Love became the first pair of college teammates to be the top two running backs selected across any draft in NFL history.

The Seahawks opted not to play Price during the preseason. Neither he nor projected backup George Holani logged any carries as Seattle looked to keep both fresh for the start of the season amid Charbonnet's injury.

Price is expected to be the lead back in Seattle's offense to open the season.

That said, it's worth noting that the Seahawks' official website actually lists Holani ahead of him on the depth chart for now. It isn't clear whether that is a product of Price not playing the preseason or if it is a reflection of the veteran being slightly ahead of the rookie entering the season.

Seattle currently has three running backs on the 53-man roster. Here's a look at the projected pecking order within that room to open the season:

Price and Holani could see a relatively even workload split early in the season. The situation could be similar to those faced by Jahmyr Gibbs and Bijan Robinson as rookies in 2023, when Gibbs shared touches with David Montgomery and Robinson did the same with Tyler Allgeier.

Whenever Charbonnet returns, he will be expected to overtake Holani in the complementary role alongside Price.

The Seahawks also have Velus Jones Jr. and Jacardia Wright on the practice squad. Both are candidates to be called up to add backfield and special teams depth, if necessary.

title: Cleveland Browns predictions for entire 2026 NFL season
description: The Browns kick off the season Sept. 13 against the Jacksonville Jaguars. So how will the season play out for them? We take a guaess here.
fullText:
BEREA ― Time to break out the crystal ball. So if you've got any problems with what follows, blame the sphere, not the writer.

The day the Browns' 2026 schedule came out, we made a knee-jerk reaction win-loss prediction on how the season would play out. The result we ended up with was a 5-12 record.

Well, four months later, with OTAs and minicamp and training camp and preseason games all having been completed to add context, we're back here to take a swing at guessing the way the season will go. This time, we're even going to throw in scores that are sure to be nowhere near what they ultimately end up being.

Well, scared money don't make any money. So let's try this again to see how the 2026 Browns season plays out.

Location, time: Everbank Stadium, 1 p.m. ET

About the game: Deshaun Watson starting for the first time since mid-October 2024. A rookie left tackle who's only played 30-some preseason game snaps in the NFL having to face two-time Pro Bowler Josh Hines-Allen in his first regular-season game. All of that against a Jaguars offense that will be in the second season under coach Liam Coen. Not necessarily the recipe for success.

Score prediction: Jaguars 30, Browns 17

Location, time: Raymond James Stadium, 1 p.m. ET

About the game: Baker Mayfield's going to have a chip on his shoulder the size of a boulder for this game. The Florida heat is going to be a factor for the second week in a row. It's a little closer, but it's still 0-2.

Score prediction: Buccaneers 24, Browns 21

Location, time: Huntington Bank Field, 1 p.m. ET

About the game: It's tempting to say this is when Shedeur Sanders makes his first start, but after two games seems a tad quick to pull the cord. This is a game where the defense gives the Browns a chance. A chance, not a win.

Score prediction: Panthers 21, Browns 20

Location, time: Huntington Bank Field, 8:20 p.m. ET

About the game: You don't make a quarterback change on the short week. Both of these teams may already want to do that by this point. The Browns ride their defense, their Thursday night success and their recent dominance over the Steelers in Cleveland to their first win.

Score prediction: Browns 24, Steelers 17

Location, time: MetLife Stadium, 1 p.m. ET

About the game: Well, can you change your starting quarterback off your first win of the season? Especially when you're going on the road to face the Jets? No, but you can after you lose to the Jets for the second time in as many years.

Score prediction: Jets 17, Browns 14

Location, time: Huntington Bank Field, 1 p.m. ET

About the game: Much like he did a year ago against the Ravens, Sanders makes a hero's debut, only this time as the starter. The Browns are going to catch one of either Baltimore or Cincinnati in Cleveland. Well, here's the one.

Score prediction: Browns 28, Ravens 27

Location, time: Nissan Stadium, 1 p.m. ET

About the game: Shedeur Sanders vs. Cam Ward Part II. This time, it's Sanders who prevails. That makes it two in a row, which is what they call a "winning streak."

Score prediction: Browns 35, Titans 28

Location, time: Acrisure Stadium, 1 p.m. ET

About the game: Nothing brings a Cleveland Browns win streak to a end quicker than a trip to Pittsburgh. Not picking a Browns win there until they actually prove they can win a game that's not being played in an empty stadium there.

Score prediction: Steelers 24, Browns 13

Location, time: Caesars Superdome, 1 p.m. ET

About the game: Another road game that could go any number of ways, just because there are any number of ways the Saints' season could go. Maybe the Browns catch the Superdome crowd a tad hung over from LSU playing Alabama the night before. Or, perhaps the Browns catch Tyler Shough continuing to rise.

Score prediction: Saints 31, Browns 21

Location, time: Huntington Bank Field, 1 p.m. ET

About the game: Remembered what the Browns defense looked like with Myles Garrett? That's what the Texans defense looks like with Will Anderson.

Score prediction: Texans 28, Browns 10

About the game: If the math is right, the Browns hit the bye week with a 3-7 record by this prediction.

Score prediction: Only prediction is a much-needed break for all involved.

Location, time: Huntington Bank Field, 1 p.m. ET

About the game: If the Browns didn't have Myles Garrett last year, there's a better than average chance Fernando Mendoza is a Cleveland Brown right now. Instead, he's on the Raiders, but it's not 100% certain he'll be starting by this point.

Score prediction: Browns 28, Raiders 20

Location, time: Huntington Bank Field, 1 p.m. ET

About the game: Already gave the Browns their one home win over either Baltimore or Cincinnati. If Garrett was still here, this one might feel 

Score prediction: Bengals 38, Browns 21

Location, time: Huntington Bank Field, 1 p.m. ET

About the game: Kevin Stefanski won a lot of games in this stadium when he was on the home sideline. Feels like he's going to win another one, only on the other sideline.

Score prediction: Falcons 24, Browns 22

Location, time: MetLife Stadium, 1 p.m. ET

About the game: Could this potentially be the Browns against yet another former quarterback of theirs? It seems doubtful that Jaxson Dart will still be healthy by this point of the season, which means it's going to be Jameis Winston time for the Giants. Cleveland goes 0-2 against the New York teams.

Score prediction: Giants 27, Browns 24

Location, time: Huntington Bank Field, 1 p.m. ET

About the game: The Ravens could be in the midst of a push for the AFC North title and a high seed in the AFC playoffs. The Browns could be pushing for the top pick in the draft.

Score prediction: Ravens 37, Browns 14

Location, time: Huntington Bank Field, 1 p.m. ET

About the game: You could say this game goes any number of different ways. So, how about this way?

Score prediction: Colts 21, Browns 17

Location, time: Paycor Stadium, Time TBD

About the game: There's so many things that could be riding on this game. Let's assume there's nothing, as was the case in this exact same spot a season ago. Let's give it the same result as last year, which gives them the same record —5-12 —as last year.

Score prediction: Browns 16, Bengals 14

title: John Cominsky details NFL retirement, new project with HOF honors next
description: Ex-Detroit Lions defensive lineman John Cominsky will be inducted into the Summit County Sports Hall of Fame and the Barberton Sports HOF this fall.
fullText:
John Cominsky has redirected the energy he needed to ascend from an underdog at Barberton High School to a starter on an NFL playoff team, using his commitment and passion to promote health education after retiring as a defensive lineman in March 2025.

Cominsky recently told the Beacon Journal he suffered "three significant" concussions as a member of the Detroit Lions in 2023. Those injuries contributed to him leaving the NFL and shifting more of his attention to assisting communities in Northeast Ohio through his Cominsky Family Foundation.

For the past six months, Cominsky has been making weekly visits to a drug and alcohol treatment center in Massillon, where he works with patients on breathing techniques and light exercise.

"It empowers an individual to see, 'Hey, if I move and breathe, I can flush this thought, I can get back to center, I can start my day off right and I can change my attitude,'" said Cominsky, who lives in Hinckley.

Watch Ohio High School Football Live on NFHS Network all year

In the meantime, Cominsky's supporters are honoring him for his on-field achievements. He will be inducted into the Summit County Sports Hall of Fame on Oct. 6 and the Barberton Sports Hall of Fame on Nov. 25.

The 30-year-old Cominsky said he's eager to celebrate his fellow inductees and express gratitude to his backers.

"I'm just proud to represent all those people that invested in me," he said.

More local sports: Summit County Sports Hall of Fame's new class has Akron Zips greats and former NFL players

Cominsky transformed from a lightly recruited jack-of-all-trades Barberton football player who quarterbacked the Magics as a senior to a 285-pound defensive end at Division II University of Charleston in West Virginia.

Eating became a job for Cominsky in college as he gained about 70 pounds and evolved into a dominant force in the trenches. He earned All-America status and the Mountain East Conference Defensive Player of the Year award en route to becoming the first Charleston player to be drafted in 68 years when the Atlanta Falcons chose him in the fourth round (No. 135 overall) in 2019.

Cominsky played five seasons in the NFL (three with the Falcons and two with the Lions) and started 20 of the 57 regular-season games in which he appeared, compiling 107 tackles, with 11 for loss and 7.5 sacks, 25 quarterback hits, a forced fumble, a fumble recovery and six passes defensed. In Cominsky's final season, he started 11 of 17 regular-season games and all three playoff games for the 2023 Lions while they made a run to the NFC championship game.

As a member of the Summit County Sports Hall of Fame's board of directors and the president of the Barberton Sports Hall of Fame, Rob Culbertson championed Cominsky's candidacy for his upcoming inductions. Culbertson was a teacher, athletic trainer and athletic director at Barberton during Cominsky's high school years.

"It is just mind-boggling that he was able to take his body and his mind and set a course for himself, set goals, and then he worked his tail off, did as his coaches told him to do, gained the weight and, lo and behold, he was able to get drafted," Culbertson said. "… He is the epitome of what the Barberton community is all about."

Cominsky hasn't forgotten his roots. He and his wife, Brittany, a fellow Barberton native, run the Cominsky Family Foundation. They have held a free youth football camp at Barberton High School for years, aided local businesses, given kids backpacks filled with non-perishable food items and delivered turkeys to pantries for Thanksgiving.

"We also are working with other organizations trying to bolster the out-of-school-time youth experience in Barberton year-round," John Cominsky said.

More John Cominsky: 'It's once in a lifetime': Barberton native helps 2023 Lions reach NFC title game

Meanwhile, health education is at the forefront of Cominsky's plans. A separate business venture in Massillon made him aware of the OVP Health Recovery Center, the drug and alcohol treatment facility where he encourages patients to breathe and move.

Cominsky calls the sessions he hosts "teatime." As an icebreaker of sorts, he wheels in a cart with hot water, tea bags and honey, offering beverages to patients who may be guarded.

"The tea is just this warm welcome," Cominsky said.

The meetings typically last for a half hour to an hour.

"I believe in meditation. I believe in breathing techniques," Cominsky said. "But when you come in with that as your spearhead, people will reject you.

"I go in and we just do basic movement and breath work. I introduce myself, 'Hey, I'm John. I believe moving and breathing is good for you. Who wants to join me?'

"It gives these people an opportunity to see the power of simple habits and routine and just how much discipline, although people see it as restricting freedom, it actually creates freedom."

About 15 to 20 people attend "teatime" each week in Massillon, Cominsky said. He has also dabbled in events with IBF Addiction Recovery in Akron.

"I've kind of wiggled my way into drug recovery without being a former addict myself, which is pretty unlikely," Cominsky said. "Even the higher-up leaders [at rehabilitation centers], a lot of them have fought addiction themselves, and so I feel grateful to have the conviction to serve this community without the history."

Cominsky said he has a desire for people to be healthy, and he wants them to prioritize health. He thought about becoming a doctor — or a pursuing another profession in the medical field — as a biology and chemistry major at Charleston. He said his enthusiasm for health and wellness would exist even if his football career had not ended the way it did, with concerns about the concussions he has endured.

"But it shines a little bit more light on it because I kind of have these lingering issues," Cominsky said. "In boxing, they call it punch-drunk. It's kind of like you have half a beer in you all the time. It's kind of like a slight vertigo. It's something I've grown used to, and it has improved.

"I have a true a gauge [for inflammation in my body] because my symptoms flare up. It's directly related to poor habits. It's directly related to if I have bad sleep, if I eat bad, if I'm dehydrated. All these things flare up."

Cominsky also suffered a torn medial collateral ligament and cartilage damage in his right knee early in the Lions' 2024 training camp. He underwent surgery and never played again in the NFL.

"I had a lot of cartilage that kind of got chipped out," he said, "almost like a golf divot right under my kneecap, and that's what was giving me most of the issues.

"I'm still dealing with things in my knee. I have a lot of cartilage missing, and it really took a while to bounce back, probably a full two years after the injury to feel 90%."

Cominsky said a silver lining is the knee injury "probably saved my brain a little bit" by sidelining him for the entire 2024 season.

As Cominsky reflected on his NFL career in 2024, he concluded the concussions from the previous year had affected his performance on the field.

"I'm looking at my game film, and I'm just watching a little bit of hesitancy," Cominsky said. "My edge when I played was that I played with my hair on fire, and I had no remorse for anything, anybody, my own body, whatever.

"I started to see myself make what they call in the NFL 'business decisions.' There's a play. The guy's probably going to go down. Just peel away. You don't have to stick your nose in there. So, I started to see these signs of like, 'Oh, buddy. Hey, you're losing your edge a little bit.'"

Of course, Cominsky thought about his future with his family, too. In 2022, he and Brittany had their first child, now 4-year-old daughter Emersyn. In 2024, Brittany became pregnant with the couple's now 1-year-old son, Wren.

"Between my family developing and the concussions that I had, I just didn't have the fire that was required of me," Cominsky said. "… I just couldn't do it, and so I was very fortunate to be able to walk away.

"It was just too many concussions, and I lost my fire. There's guys out there with fire times a hundred, and you don't want to be on the same field as somebody who is all in when you're not 100% in. So, it was time."

Cominsky turned to a new chapter, and he plans to write many more.

"I'm pretty set on this health education piece and bringing that to all people, including vulnerable populations," he said.

The Summit County Sport Hall of Fame's 68th induction ceremony and banquet will be held on Tuesday, Oct. 6, at Annunciation Greek Orthodox Church, 129 S. Union St., Akron. Doors are scheduled to open at 5:15 p.m. A social/cocktail hour is slated to run from 5:30-6:30 p.m. The program and dinner are set to start at 6:30 p.m.

In addition to Cominsky, this year's SCSHOF inductees are James Eberwine (rifle), Doran Grant (football), John Groce (basketball coach), Jeff Howard (cross country and track and field coach), Whitney Mercilus (football), Hope Murphy (cross country and track) and Rachel Tecca-Fleming (basketball).

Rosemary "Rosie" Hickin will receive the Ed Kalail Volunteer Award. Ray Yannucci will receive the Andy Palich Memorial Service Award.

Tickets can be purchased online at summitcountyshof.org/purchase-tickets. Tickets for adults are $75. Tickets for children (12 and younger) are $25. Patron tickets are $90 and include the purchaser's name in the banquet program. A table of eight is $550. A table of 10 is $700.

For information on advertising in the banquet program or event sponsorship opportunities, contact SCSHOF board of directors President Jeff Kurtz at 330-329-3677 or SCSHOF board of directors Vice President Glenda Buchanan at 330-687-1896.

The Barberton Sport Hall of Fame's 48th banquet will be held on Wednesday, Nov. 25, at Al's Corner Restaurant, 155 2nd St. NW, Barberton. A cocktail hour is set to start at 5:30 p.m. with dinner at 6:30 p.m.

Tickets can be purchased by mailing a check or money order to the Barberton Sports Hall of Fame P.O. Box 214 Barberton, OH, 44203. Tickets are $60 for adults and $20 for children. Checks or money orders should be made payable to the Barberton Sports Hall of Fame.

In addition to Cominsky, this year's Barberton Sports Hall of Fame inductees will be Culbertson (athletic trainer), Shana Andrus (basketball), Rohn Noirot (football) and Cobey Fehr (wrestling).

George Krska will receive the O.C. Barber Award. Kevin Pletcher will receive the Chuck Ebner President's Award.

title: Utd goal v Ipswich backed by league panel despite Maguire handball
description: The decision to allow a Manchester United goal against Ipswich after a handball by Harry Maguire has been backed by the Premier League’s Key Match Incidents (KMI) Panel – though one panellist felt the handball was deliberate. The ball appeared to come off Maguire’s hand as he controlled it just outside the penalty area during the match on August 30.
fullText:
The decision to allow a Manchester United goal against Ipswich after a handball by Harry Maguire has been backed by the Premier League's Key Match Incidents (KMI) Panel – though one panellist felt the handball was deliberate.

The ball appeared to come off Maguire's hand as he controlled it just outside the penalty area during the match on August 30. He then unleashed a shot, which was going wide before being deflected in by Jacob Greaves in United's 5-2 win.

The handball was deemed to be accidental by both referee Craig Pawson and VAR Jarred Gillett, and because Maguire's shot did not go in directly, that meant the goal was allowed to stand.

The KMI Panel is an independent group comprised of three former players or coaches, one Premier League representative and one from officiating body Pro Ref. Panel findings on key incidents in every game-week are being published this season for the first time.

The panel said on Wednesday: "Maguire's arms are within his bodyline, meaning that the contact with his right arm was accidental and not a punishable handball offence given that Maguire was not the goal scorer.

"The shot was clearly off-target and then deflected in via the defender for a clear own goal. The panel supported the referee's call to award the goal, 4:1, with one panellist considering the handball to be deliberate."

On the day of the match, the Premier League's Match Centre account on X posted: "The referee's call of goal for Manchester United was checked and confirmed by VAR – with it deemed that Maguire was not the immediate goalscorer after an accidental handball."

The same post also quoted the VAR: "It's an own goal and the accidental handball is not punishable, so we recommend you award the goal."

title: Who will be 'College GameDay' guest picker for Texas-Ohio State? Potential Week 2 choices
description: Who will be the guest picker for ESPN's "College GameDay" in Week 2? Here are some options when the show visits Texas-Ohio State in Austin, Texas:
fullText:
The college football world turns its attention to a matchup between top-three ranked teams when No. 3 Texas hosts No. 1 Ohio State in Week 2 with ESPN's "College GameDay" on deck.

It's the second matchup of a home-and-home series that started last season with Ohio State's 14-7 win in a low-scoring affair. Both Julian Sayin and Arch Manning made their debuts as full-time starters in the game, and have both blossomed into two of the best signal-callers in college football since their shaky starts.

REQUIRED READING: Notre Dame leads reshuffled college football NCAA Re-Rank 1-138 after Week 1

Texas, of course, gives ESPN plenty of celebrities and former sports icons to choose from to be the celebrity guest picker. The second-largest school in Texas, the largest state in the continental United States, is not only one of the top public schools in the nation but also one of the most historically impressive in athletics.

Who will the celebrity guest picker be when "College GameDay" visits Austin, Texas? Here's a look at some potential options:

Academy Award-winning actor Matthew McConaughey is the obvious choice, almost never missing his alma mater's games. The football team's "minister of culture" also teaches a film class at Texas.

McConaughey is already also appearing in the media ahead of Texas-Ohio State, talking to Scott Van Pelt on ESPN's "SportsCenter" on Sept. 7. He already once appeared on "GameDay" back in 2019, but it seems about time for the fan favorite to come back on the show.

“It’s between the ears of more of these young men on this football team, the belief that this is the time to do it.”@McConaughey speaks with @notthefakeSVP about the expectations on Texas football and the team’s belief 🏈 pic.twitter.com/zS0eDjPJse

Why not invite Arch Manning's Super Bowl-winning uncles? Arch Manning is the latest Manning star in the family of quarterbacks, and Arch is expected to be a first-round pick in the NFL draft like his uncles, too.

ESPN might want to include Arch Manning's dad, Cooper Manning, in the festivities, too — but getting Eli and Peyton Manning, who star in numerous ESPN productions alongside each other, would be a huge hit among fans.

Former Texas star Vince Young led the Longhorns to their most recent national championship in 2005 after scoring one of the most iconic touchdowns in college football history. Young has never been the guest picker on "College GameDay," but he would be a smart choice by the pregame show, given his legendary status in Texas' history.

Kevin Durant only spent one season at Texas, but it might've been the school's single-best campaign in program history. The NBA legend has never been shy of boasting his Texas fandom, and he would be a nice get for "College GameDay."

Scottie Scheffler is the No. 1-ranked golfer in the world, and just so happened to attend Texas. The Texas native might not be the likeliest choice since he appeared on the show in 2024, but he's a very relevant sports icon connected to the school.

Scheffler has 22 career PGA Tour wins, two of which were Masters Tournament victories in 2022 and 2024.

title: 2 new signings join Arsenal u19 squad to face Napoli
description: The provisional Arsenal u19 squad to face Napoli in Wednesday’s UEFA Youth League clash has been released, with new signings Axel Donczew and Igor Tyjon looking to debut.Photo via Arsenal.comUEFA ha...
fullText:
UEFA have published Arsenal's provisional squad list for Wednesday's UEFA Youth League opener against Napoli, with new signings Axel Donczew and Igor Tyjon both included.

Tyjon completed his long-awaited transfer to Arsenal from Blackburn Rovers in late August, signing professional terms with his new club and taking the number 64.

Donczew then joined Arsenal from Cardiff City later that same week, signing a scholarship deal with a pre-contract agreement for professional terms when he turns 17. He's taken the number 80.

Neither players has yet had the chance to debut for the Arsenal academy, so they may get their first opportunity on Wednesday.

Other notable inclusions are Brayden Clarke and Andre Harriman-Annous, who are both over the age limit for the Youth League.

Teams are allowed up to five players who are up to one year older than the limit, though those players must have been registered with the club for at least two years to qualify. Clarke signed in March 2024, so he now fits that requirement.

It's also worth mentioning Luis Munoz (14) and Jaden Maghoma (15), who are both still schoolboys and younger than many of their teammates for the game.

U21 boss David Horseman will lead the team, so it seems he's set to remain in charge of the u19s in the Youth League despite his full-time appointment to the u21s.

fullText:
PSG have an impressive ten players shortlisted for the Ballon d'Or this year, with a few very good candidates for the award.

If you enjoy PSG Talk coverage and want to see more of it, add us as a preferred source on Google to make us a favourite and see more of our content.

September is here, and that means the return of the tedious Ballon d'Or campaigning season.

The nominees for the 2026 Men's edition are out, and of course there are a host of PSG players in there – ten of the thirty, to be precise:

Ousmane Dembélé, Khvicha Kvaratskhelia, Ferran Torres, Vitinha, Fabian Ruiz, João Neves, Nuno Mendes, Achraf Hakimi, Willian Pacho and Marquinhos are all on the shortlist. Nine of them were on the list last season as the Parisians won their second Champions League in a row.

Missing out is goalkeeper Matvey Safonov, Desire Doue, and poor Warren Zaire-Emery, who can't seem to get the respect he deserves anywhere.

Fabian Ruiz is the only player to have won the World Cup and Champions League, while others have suggested that Kvaratskhelia should win it, rather than be punished for the fact that Georgia didn't go to World Cup.

There are many worthy potential winners on that list.

PSG's winless start to the season meant some very poor marks for the majority of the team as they lost to Monaco at the weekend.

As you can see above, the form of Matvey Safonov has been a concern to start the season – he's just not been at his best, conceding 6 from 9 shots on target.

It's been a slow start to the season in terms of results, but the situation around summer signing Lucas Digne is much more concerning than that.

fullText:
Chelsea's midfield situation – a little short while Moises Caicedo is out – has led to links to other players who could be signed.

If you enjoy Talk Chelsea coverage and want to see more of it, add us as a preferred source on Google to make us a favourite and see more of our content.

TeamTalk have just put out an exclusive which claims that Chelsea are going to reignite their interest in Arsenal midfielder Martin Zubimendi in January.

The former Real Sociedad man has not made himself a weekly starter for the Gunners, and there are whispers he would like to move on to a team where he's a key player. Chelsea are short in midfield at the moment with the likes of Moises Caicedo and Jordan Henderson out.

There was chatter before the deadline that Zubimendi was on the Blues' shortlist.

Martin Zubimendi (Photo by Florencia Tan Jun/Getty Images)

title: What to know about Ryan Garcia's WBC title fight defense vs Conor Benn

fullText:

title: What Lane Kiffin book reveals about Ole Miss departure, wanting Trinidad Chambliss at LSU
description: The Clarion Ledger got a review copy of "Lane Being Lane," John Talty's book about former Ole Miss coach Lane Kiffin now at LSU.
fullText:
OXFORD — A new book attempts to answer the Lane Kiffin question Ole Miss football fans asked repeatedly during his dramatic departure last year.

"Lane Being Lane" is the third college football book from John Talty, who was a Clarion Ledger recruiting writer from 2012-14. It will release Sept. 15, shortly before Kiffin and LSU are scheduled to return to Oxford in Week 3 for a game against Ole Miss on Sept. 19 (6:30 p.m., ABC).

Talty provided the Clarion Ledger with an advance copy. Kiffin did not participate directly in the book.

"I want to just dive super deep into who this guy is and why he does the things he does," Talty told the Clarion Ledger. "Like, how did he get here? Why does he do these things?"

The book presents a look at Kiffin's life, starting from his childhood and finishing after Kiffin went to LSU on Nov. 30, 2025. Fans will read a comprehensive recount of the bitter split between Kiffin and Ole Miss.

Right before Kiffin's departure, a source in the book likens Kiffin's behavior during a meeting with Ole Miss Athletic Director Keith Carter and Chancellor Glenn Boyce to that of a "kid having a temper tantrum." The meeting was about if Kiffin would be allowed to coach in the College Football Playoff. It was supposed to take 10 minutes. It lasted two hours.

"I think for the first time ever he finally heard Keith Carter say no," Ole Miss booster Smitty Smith says in the book.

The book details how Kiffin contacted sports attorney Tom Mars late in the 2025 season to fight for quarterback Trinidad Chambliss' eligibility. As time wore on and Kiffin left for LSU, Mars details how Kiffin asked for updates via text or calls several times per day.

"It was clear to me — it would be cleat to anyone except the village idiot — that he was hoping the appeal would be granted so he could bring Trinidad to LSU," Mars said.

Talty writes that, despite Kiffin's public support of his former team, Kiffin was "despondent" when Ole Miss beat Georgia in the College Football Playoff without him. Talty includes a story from an unnamed close friend of Kiffin's.

"It was killing him. He was texting us non-stop during the game. Sends me ... a picture of (Ole Miss running back) Kewan Lacy in an LSU uniform dunking on Ole Miss during the (expletive) game."

In the book, that friend later said Kiffin "lost his mind" when Lacy committed to return to Ole Miss. The book goes on to detail about how Kiffin egged on Clemson coach Dabo Swinney to report Ole Miss tampering for transfer linebacker Luke Ferrelli. Swinney has since denied it.

One of the book's themes is how polarizing Kiffin is.

"You could ask fifty guys about Lane and they would say he was an arrogant asshole," high school football teammate Casey Elder said in the book. "Fifty other guys would say, 'What a great guy.' He was cocky and confident but a good guy, I fell into that camp."

The book traces how a laundry list of revered figures have shaped Kiffin's career: His father Monte Kiffin, former USC coach Pete Carroll, former Alabama coach Nick Saban and agent Jimmy Sexton. There are also stories about little-known people who helped make Kiffin, including his high school football coach and childhood friends.

Kiffin's time as a mischievous high school football player is revisited, and his days as a young, sometimes brash assistant coach climbing the coach ladder at USC with Ed Orgeron and Steve Sarkisian. Kiffin's time as the head coach of the Oakland Raiders is, fittingly, just one chapter.

Ole Miss fans will find Talty's recount of Kiffin's six years in Oxford fascinating. There are highs, like the 2023 Chick-fil-A Peach Bowl win over Penn State (the final game Kiffin had with his father) and when Ole Miss beat Georgia on a rainy Oxford night in 2024.

There are also lows. It's not a gossipy book, but it doesn't shy away from Kiffin's off-the-field struggles. High-level Ole Miss boosters are interviewed. So is a licensed psychologist who specializes in sexual addiction, and a bar employee in Tuscaloosa, Alabama.

The book recounts when Kiffin, who did not have personal private plane usage in his first Ole Miss contract, grumbled about it. When an Ole Miss donor set him up with an $8 million King Air private plane, Kiffin reportedly sent some donors a text of a photo of himself in the plane describing it as a "piece of (expletive)."

When Ole Miss and LSU play, Kiffin's return will be a fascinating look at a hero-turned-villain in his old home. It will be the latest example of why Talty chose his tagline for the book: College football's Agent of Chaos.

"He's just had such a fascinating one of one coaching career," Talty said. "Like truly, no one else has had a coaching career like this guy."

Sam Hutchens covers Ole Miss for the Clarion Ledger. Email him at Shutchens@gannett.com or reach him on X at @Sam_Hutchens_

John Talty will sign his book "Lane Being Lane" at Off Square Books in Oxford on Sept. 16 at 5:30 p.m. and Lemuria Books in Jackson on Sept. 17 at 5 p.m.

fullText:

The Delray Beach, Florida, native must first tackle her match in the tournament quarterfinals, which she has reached for the first time since winning in Flushing Meadows in 2023. But her opponent will likely be her toughest competition to date in the tournament, as the fourth-seeded Gauff takes on fifth-seed Mirra Andreeva from Russia.

The 22-year-old Gauff needed only 93 minutes to dispatch of No. 14 seed Iva Jovic, 6-1, 6-4, on Sept. 7, winning 73% of the net points and recording only two aces. But at only 19, Andreeva already has a Grand Slam under her belt after she won this year's French Open.
